1003	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1004	# Generator — PROMPTS is the single source of truth; render the prompt blocks
1005	# in .chezmoi.toml.tmpl + Dockerfile from it. `gen --check` (pre-commit/CI)
1006	# fails if the on-disk files drift.
1007	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1008	
1009	# Marker pairs delimiting the regions `gen` owns. Everything outside them is
1010	# hand-authored (umask, $profile setup, [diff]/[status], the RUN prefix, etc.).
1011	TMPL_BEGIN = "# >>> dotfiles-init:prompts (generated by scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py gen) — DO NOT EDIT BY HAND >>>"
1012	TMPL_END = "# <<< dotfiles-init:prompts <<<"
1013	DOCKER_ARGS_BEGIN = "# >>> dotfiles-init:args (generated by scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py gen) — DO NOT EDIT BY HAND >>>"
1014	DOCKER_ARGS_END = "# <<< dotfiles-init:args <<<"
1015	DOCKER_RUN_BEGIN = "# >>> dotfiles-init:init-run (generated by scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py gen) — DO NOT EDIT BY HAND >>>"
1016	DOCKER_RUN_END = "# <<< dotfiles-init:init-run <<<"
1017	README_BEGIN = "<!-- dotfiles-init:prompts (coverage-checked by scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py gen --check) -->"
1018	README_END = "<!-- /dotfiles-init:prompts -->"
1019	
1020	# Docker devbox build defaults — deliberately leaner than the prompt defaults
1021	# so the CI image builds fast (skip the heavy coding-agent / uv / js installs,
1022	# no backup). Anything not listed uses the prompt's own default.
1023	DOCKER_ARG_DEFAULTS: dict[str, object] = {
1024	    "installCodingAgents": False,
1025	    "installPythonUvTools": False,
1026	    "installJsCliTools": False,
1027	    "installExtraRuntimes": False,  # skip ~1.8GB of mise runtimes in CI images
1028	    "backupMode": "off",
1029	    "discordChannel": "none",
1030	}
1031	# Basics get Docker-specific placeholder identities.
1032	DOCKER_BASICS: dict[str, str] = {
1033	    "profile": "ubuntu_server",
1034	    "email": "docker@example.com",
1035	    "name": "Docker User",
1036	}
1037	
1038	
1039	def _key_to_arg(key: str) -> str:
1040	    """camelCase chezmoi key -> CHEZMOI_UPPER_SNAKE Docker ARG name."""
1041	    return "CHEZMOI_" + re.sub(r"(?<!^)(?=[A-Z])", "_", key).upper()
1042	
1043	
1044	def _prompt_once_call(p: Prompt) -> str:
1045	    """The `{{ promptXOnce ... }}` assignment value for a prompt."""
1046	    if p.kind == "bool":
1047	        return "{{ promptBoolOnce . \"%s\" \"%s\" %s }}" % (
1048	            p.key, p.prompt_text, "true" if p.default else "false")
1049	    if p.kind == "choice":
1050	        choices = " ".join('"%s"' % c for c in p.choices)
1051	        return "{{ promptChoiceOnce . \"%s\" \"%s\" (list %s) \"%s\" | quote }}" % (
1052	            p.key, p.prompt_text, choices, p.default)
1053	    return "{{ promptStringOnce . \"%s\" \"%s\" \"%s\" | quote }}" % (
1054	        p.key, p.prompt_text, p.default)
1055	
1056	
1057	def _go_literal(kind: PromptType, value: object) -> str:
1058	    """Render an else_value as a TOML literal baked into the template."""
1059	    if kind == "bool":
1060	        return "true" if value else "false"
1061	    return '"%s"' % value
1062	
1063	
1064	def render_tmpl_body() -> str:
1065	    """Render the generated .chezmoi.toml.tmpl prompt block (non-hidden prompts)."""
1066	    lines: list[str] = []
1067	    for p in PROMPTS:
1068	        if p.hidden:
1069	            continue
1070	        for cl in p.comment.split("\n") if p.comment else []:
1071	            lines.append(("# " + cl).rstrip())
1072	        assign = "%s = %s" % (p.key, _prompt_once_call(p))
1073	        if p.condition is None:
1074	            lines.append(assign)
1075	        else:
1076	            lines.append("{{ if %s -}}" % p.condition.to_go())
1077	            lines.append(assign)
1078	            lines.append("{{ else -}}")
1079	            lines.append("%s = %s" % (p.key, _go_literal(p.kind, p.else_value)))

1129	    pattern = re.compile(re.escape(begin) + r"\n.*?\n" + re.escape(end), re.DOTALL)
1130	    replacement = begin + "\n" + body + "\n" + end
1131	    new_text, n = pattern.subn(lambda _m: replacement, text)
1132	    if n != 1:

1402	def _coerce_set_value(p: Prompt, raw: str) -> object:
1403	    """Coerce a --set string value to the prompt's type, raising ValueError on
1404	    a bad bool token or an out-of-range choice."""
1405	    if p.kind == "bool":
1406	        low = raw.strip().lower()
1407	        if low in _TRUE_TOKENS:
1408	            return True
1409	        if low in _FALSE_TOKENS:
1410	            return False
1411	        raise ValueError(f"{p.key}: expected a bool (true/false), got {raw!r}")
1412	    if p.kind == "choice":
1413	        if raw not in p.choices:
1414	            raise ValueError(f"{p.key}: {raw!r} not in {list(p.choices)}")
1415	        return raw
1416	    return raw

1419	def parse_set_overrides(pairs: tuple[str, ...]) -> dict[str, object]:
1420	    """Parse `--set key=value` pairs into a typed override dict, validating
1421	    each key against PROMPTS. Raises SystemExit with a friendly message on any
1422	    unknown key or bad value."""
1423	    by_key = {p.key: p for p in PROMPTS}
1424	    out: dict[str, object] = {}
1425	    for pair in pairs:
1426	        if "=" not in pair:
1427	            raise SystemExit(f"--set expects key=value, got {pair!r}")
1428	        key, raw = pair.split("=", 1)
1429	        key = key.strip()
1430	        if key not in by_key:
1431	            raise SystemExit(
1432	                f"--set: unknown key {key!r}. Valid keys: "
1433	                + ", ".join(p.key for p in PROMPTS)
1434	            )
1435	        try:
1436	            out[key] = _coerce_set_value(by_key[key], raw)
1437	        except ValueError as e:
1438	            raise SystemExit(f"--set: {e}")
1439	    return out

### 3. **`fleet exec` — Shell Function Sourcing & PATH Prelude**

**Files involved:**
- `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/scripts/fleet/exec.py` (lines 176–180)
- `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_fleet` (lines 237–239)

**The `_PATH_PRELUDE` constant** (exec.py, lines 176–180):

```python
_PATH_PRELUDE = (
    "$HOME/.dotfiles/bin:$HOME/.cargo/bin:$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/bin:"
    "/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin:"
    "$HOME/.linuxbrew/bin:$PATH"
)
```

**How `fleet exec` runs commands:**

From the docstring (lines 1–20):
> 1. Default: argv list after `--`, **no shell expansion** (safe by construction).
> 2. `--shell <bin>` opt-in: wraps in `<bin> -c '<argv joined>'` so the user can use pipes / globs / redirects.
> 3. `--login` opt-in: wraps in `<shell> -lc '...'` so the remote rc files load (gives access to nvm / mise / conda / **aliases**).

**Decision matrix** (lines 183–213, `_build_remote_cmd` function):

```python
# Non-login, no shell → PATH prelude + exec <quoted argv>
# --shell bin (no login) → PATH prelude + <bin> -c '<argv-joined>'
# --shell bin + --login → <bin> -lc '<argv-joined>' (no PATH prelude, rc files load PATH)
# --login only → bash -lc <quoted argv> (no PATH prelude)
```

**Answer: Are sourced shell functions available to `fleet exec`?**

**It depends on the mode:**

1. **Default mode (`fleet exec -- CMD`):** NO. Only executables in `$PATH` are available. The remote shell is **non-interactive** and the user's rc files (where functions are sourced) are **not loaded**. Each arg is shlex-quoted, so pipes/globs won't expand either.

2. **With `--login` flag:** YES, if the function is in a standard rc file (`~/.bashrc`, `~/.zshrc`). The login shell loads all rc files, sourcing `dot_config/shell/*.sh` where your function would live.

3. **With `--shell bash` (no login):** NO by default. Shell expansion works (pipes, globs), but rc files aren't loaded. However, the `_PATH_PRELUDE` is still injected, so functions aren't available **unless they're already compiled into the shell binary or exported as aliases.**

**To use `fleet exec` with a shell function across hosts:**

```bash
# Option A: Use --login so rc files load
fleet exec --login -- sysmute toggle

# Option B: Inline the function definition (for non-interactive usage)
fleet exec -- sh -c 'sysmute_body() { ... }; sysmute_body toggle'

# Option C: Make it an executable in ~/.dotfiles/bin/ (symlink or wrapper)
# Then it appears in $PATH via the _PATH_PRELUDE
```

**PATH prelude details:**
- Order is intentional: **package managers win over ~/bin** (cargo → uv → brew order ensures reproducibility)
- **Deliberately diverges from interactive shell PATH** (which prioritizes ~/bin) to avoid legacy ~/bin shadowing modern tools
- Applied **only when NOT login** (login shells load PATH from rc files, so augmentation is redundant)

```text
# 55_web_reader.sh - Render web pages as markdown in the terminal (shared).
# Moved from dot_config/zsh/tools/55_web_reader.zsh; `print -u2` → `printf >&2`
# and `__zsh_reader_require` renamed to `__reader_require` to drop the
# misleading zsh prefix.
#
# Four extractors, pick by function name:
#   readurl   - jina.ai Reader (remote, zero local deps beyond glow)
#   readlocal - trafilatura (local, Python; offline article extraction)
#   readnode  - readability-cli / `readable` (local, Node; Mozilla Readability)
#   readraw   - curl + pandoc (full page -> GFM; no article extraction)
#
# All wrap the underlying fetch in `try_direct_then_proxy` from 50_networking.sh,
# so non-GFW'd URLs pay zero proxy overhead and only fall back if direct fetch fails.

# Normalize URL: prepend https:// if scheme missing.
_norm_url() {
  local url="$1"
  if [[ "$url" != http://* && "$url" != https://* ]]; then
    url="https://$url"
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$url"
}

# Missing-binary guard: print a one-line install hint and return 127.
__reader_require() {
  local bin="$1" hint="$2"
  if ! command -v "$bin" &>/dev/null; then
    printf '%s\n' "$bin not found -- install: $hint" >&2
    return 127
  fi
```
</details></tool-use>

129	# === Target Python interpreter override (CentOS 7 + similar) ===
130	#
131	# ansible-core 2.18+ modules wrap themselves in `from __future__ import
132	# annotations` (Py3.7+ syntax). When ansible runs against a target whose
133	# auto-discovered `/usr/bin/python3` is older (CentOS 7 ships 3.6.8),
134	# every task fails at the Gathering Facts stage with:
135	#   SyntaxError: future feature annotations is not defined
136	#
137	# Detect the auto-discovered python's version; if < 3.7, fall back to
138	# uv's managed python (already pulled into ~/.local/share/uv/python/...
139	# by `uv tool install ansible-core` in bootstrap) and pass it via
140	# -e ansible_python_interpreter. This is forward-compatible: on Rocky 9
141	# (Py 3.9+) the override is unnecessary and the if-branch is skipped.
142	#
143	# See pitfalls/centos7-noroot.md → "controller Python pin" for the
144	# matching controller-side fix; this is the target-side companion.
145	ANSIBLE_PY_INTERP=""
146	detect_target_python() {
147	    local sys_py="${1:-/usr/bin/python3}"
148	    if ! [[ -x "$sys_py" ]]; then
149	        return 1
150	    fi
151	    local sys_ver
152	    sys_ver="$("$sys_py" -c 'import sys; print(f"{sys.version_info.major}.{sys.version_info.minor}")' 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
153	    # Pure-bash version comparison: Python is fine if >= 3.7
154	    awk -v v="$sys_ver" 'BEGIN { split(v, a, "."); exit !(a[1]>3 || (a[1]==3 && a[2]>=7)) }'
155	}
156	if ! detect_target_python; then
157	    # Find a Python 3.10+ via uv (controller used --python 3.13 by bootstrap).
158	    # Search uv's managed python dir + falls back to `uv python find` if uv is on PATH.
159	    UV_PY_CANDIDATE=""
160	    for cand in "$HOME"/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.13.*-linux-*/bin/python3 \
161	                "$HOME"/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.12.*-linux-*/bin/python3 \
162	                "$HOME"/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.11.*-linux-*/bin/python3 \
163	                "$HOME"/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.10.*-linux-*/bin/python3; do
164	        if [[ -x "$cand" ]]; then
165	            UV_PY_CANDIDATE="$cand"
166	            break
167	        fi
168	    done
169	    if [[ -z "$UV_PY_CANDIDATE" ]] && command -v uv &> /dev/null; then
170	        UV_PY_CANDIDATE="$(uv python find 3.13 2>/dev/null || uv python find 3.12 2>/dev/null || uv python find 3.11 2>/dev/null || uv python find 3.10 2>/dev/null)"
171	    fi
172	    if [[ -n "$UV_PY_CANDIDATE" && -x "$UV_PY_CANDIDATE" ]]; then
173	        ANSIBLE_PY_INTERP="$UV_PY_CANDIDATE"
174	        info "System python3 < 3.7; using uv-managed Python at $ANSIBLE_PY_INTERP"
175	    else
176	        warn "System python3 < 3.7 and no uv-managed python found; ansible Gathering Facts may fail"
177	        warn "Manual fallback: \`uv python install 3.13 && chezmoi apply\`"
178	    fi
179	fi

320	# === Handle sudo (delegated to scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh) ==================
321	# The helper (sudo_session_init) is idempotent: if bootstrap already prompted
322	# the user and spawned the watchdog, this call just re-exports the env vars.
323	# If ansible is run standalone (bypassing bootstrap), it prompts here instead.
324	#
325	# After init we classify via sudo_session_skip_reason:
326	#   "cached"           -> pass $CHEZMOI_ANSIBLE_BECOME_FILE to ansible via -e @
327	#   "passwordless"     -> no become password needed
328	#   "non-interactive"  -> caller-specific fallback (below)
329	# Importantly we DO NOT run `sudo -k` here anymore — doing so would throw away
330	# the bootstrap-era cache and force a second prompt for the ansible phase.
331	BECOME_FLAGS=""
332	{{ if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" -}}

341	if [[ "$NEED_SUDO" == "1" ]]; then
342	    if sudo_session_init "ansible"; then
343	        case "$(sudo_session_skip_reason)" in
344	            cached)
345	                # Refresh the current TTY's sudo timestamp so the cask child
346	                # `sudo /usr/sbin/installer` finds a live ticket (it does not
347	                # accept a piped password). The watchdog keeps it warm every 50s.
348	                sudo_session_warm_cache || warn "sudo_session_warm_cache failed; pkg casks may still prompt"
349	                ;;
350	            passwordless)
351	                info "Passwordless sudo detected"
352	                ;;
353	            non-interactive | "")
354	                warn "Non-interactive mode without passwordless sudo - pkg-based casks may be skipped"
355	                ;;
356	        esac
357	    else
358	        warn "Sudo session could not be established - pkg-based casks may be skipped"
359	    fi
360	fi
361	{{ end -}}
362	{{ else -}}
363	{{ $noRoot := false }}{{ if hasKey . "noRoot" }}{{ $noRoot = .noRoot }}{{ end -}}
364	{{ if $noRoot -}}
365	# noRoot mode: skip all sudo-requiring tasks, user-level fallbacks will install tools
366	info "noRoot mode enabled - installing user-level tools to ~/.local/bin"
367	info ""
368	info "The following tools will be installed without sudo:"
369	info "  neovim, fzf, lazygit, gh, diffnav, ripgrep, fd, jq, just, bat, eza, delta,"
370	info "  yazi, zellij, btop, gitleaks, zoxide, tldr, pre-commit, thefuck,"
371	info "  duckdb, rclone, litellm, llmfit, models"
372	info ""
373	info "The following tools require sudo (ask your administrator):"
374	info "  git, curl, wget, zsh, tmux, htop, direnv, build-essential, docker, ollama"
375	info ""
376	info "Suggested command for your administrator:"
377	info "  sudo apt install git curl wget zsh tmux htop direnv build-essential tree"
378	info ""
379	BECOME_FLAGS="--skip-tags sudo"
380	# Ruby can't compile without libffi-dev (requires sudo on Ubuntu)
381	TAGS="${TAGS//,ruby_gem_tools/}"

396	        EXTRA_VARS="niri_no_root=true"
397	    else
398	        EXTRA_VARS="$EXTRA_VARS niri_no_root=true"
399	    fi
400	fi
401	{{ if $installLlmTools -}}

404	else
405	    EXTRA_VARS="$EXTRA_VARS llm_tools_no_root=true"
406	fi
407	{{ end -}}
408	{{ else -}}
409	# Non-noRoot Linux: the shared helper gives us one of three outcomes.
410	if ! sudo_session_init "ansible"; then
411	    warn "Non-interactive mode without passwordless sudo and no /dev/tty access"

1	# Custom Aliases & Shell Functions
2	
3	Quick reference for custom aliases and shell functions defined in this dotfiles repo. Available in zsh, bash, or both — the source file path tells you which:
4	
5	- `dot_config/shell/*.sh` — POSIX layer, sourced by **both** `~/.zshrc` and `~/.bashrc`.
6	- `dot_config/zsh/*.zsh` (or `tools/*.zsh`) — **zsh-only**.
7	- `dot_config/bash/*.bash` — **bash-only**.

457	## Session Management
458	
459	> `sesh-*` requires `sesh` + `tmux`; `tsesh` also requires the `try-cli` Ruby gem. `mrun` / `tmrun` / `zjrun` only need tmux or zellij (whichever backend is selected) — no sesh dependency.
460	
461	| Command | Type | Source File | Description |
462	|---------|------|-------------|-------------|
463	| `sesh-sessions` | function | `dot_config/shell/22_sesh.sh` (zsh widget: `dot_config/zsh/tools/22_sesh.zsh`; bash ble.sh binding: `dot_config/bash/06_sesh.bash.tmpl`) | fzf popup picker for all sesh sessions (also bound to `Alt+S` in both shells) |
464	| `sesh-here` / `shere` | function / alias | `dot_config/shell/22_sesh.sh` | Lightweight: bare shell session at `$PWD` (no nvim, no project layout). Pass args/`-c CMD` to override |
465	| `sesh-root` / `sroot` | function / alias | `dot_config/shell/22_sesh.sh` | Connect sesh to current git root (falls back to `$PWD`); honors sesh.toml wildcards/default |
466	| `sesh-code` / `scode` | function / alias | `dot_config/shell/22_sesh.sh` | Repo-scoped coding-agent layout: nvim 75% \| `specstory run [agent]` 25%, plus btop window. Session named `coding-agent/<repo>` (collision-safe). Refuses outside git repos. Flags: `--on-exit shell\|kill\|restart`, `--no-specstory` |
467	| `sesh-vibe` / `svibe` | function / alias | `dot_config/shell/22_sesh.sh` | Parametric multi-agent layout: `svibe [N] [CLI]` (homogeneous) or `svibe --agents claude,codex,opencode,…` (heterogeneous). N tiled agent panes + lazygit window + nvim window. Session named `vibe/<repo>`. Same `--on-exit` / `--no-specstory` flags as scode. Requires bash 4+ when invoked from bash |
468	| `try-sesh` / `tsesh` | function / alias | `dot_config/zsh/tools/32_try.zsh` | Open a `try` ephemeral workspace and immediately connect via sesh |
469	| `mrun` | function | `dot_config/zsh/tools/23_mrun.zsh` | Fire-and-forget: detached tmux/zellij session running CMD at `$PWD`, returns immediately. `mrun [-b tmux\|zellij] [-n NAME] [-d DIR] [-f] [--on-exit shell\|kill\|restart] [-k] [--] CMD [ARGS...]`. Default `--on-exit shell` keeps the session alive after CMD exits (drops to login shell, re-run via history-Up); `-k` restores fire-and-forget kill semantics. Backend default tmux (override via `$MRUN_BACKEND`). Soft-warns on TUI commands. Prints attach hint to stderr |
470	| `tmrun` | function | `dot_config/zsh/tools/23_mrun.zsh` | `mrun -b tmux`. Detached tmux session running CMD; attach with `tmux attach -t NAME` |
471	| `zjrun` | function | `dot_config/zsh/tools/23_mrun.zsh` | `mrun -b zellij`. Generates ephemeral KDL under `$TMPDIR/mrun-layout-*` (with `default_tab_template` so the standard tab-bar / status-bar plugins are restored), spawns detached zellij session; attach with `zellij attach NAME` |

557	### Proxy helpers
558	
559	> Portable loopback-proxy helpers. Honors `$LOCAL_PROXY_URL` (+ optional `$LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL` for split Clash `socks-port:` configs); otherwise prefers an active Clash config (`mixed-port:` or `port:`/`socks-port:` from `~/.config/clash/config.yaml` or `~/Library/Application Support/clash/config.yaml`) before falling back to probing ports 7890/7891/1087/8118/8080 with `nc -z -w1`. Detection is cached per shell; `proxy-off` and `proxy-refresh` clear that cache before the next lookup. Set `$LOCAL_PROXY_AUTO_ACTIVATE=1` to auto-export env vars on shell startup. Full guide: [docs/tools/web-reader.md](../tools/web-reader.md). See also: [docs/tools/containers.md](../tools/containers.md) for how `$LOCAL_PROXY_URL` feeds the chezmoi-managed `~/.docker/config.json` `proxies.default` block.

 `./docs/zsh/zsh-completions.md`

```text
1	# Zsh & Bash Completions
2	
3	How tab completions are organized in this dotfiles project — for both upstream tools and in-house CLIs (`fleet`, `mlf`, `pqsum`, `mi-router`, `x`).
4	
5	## How autocomplete works (mechanics)
6	
7	Tab completion is the same idea on both shells but the plumbing differs.
8	
9	### zsh — `compinit` + `fpath` + autoload `_<tool>` functions
10	
11	1. **`compinit`** scans every directory in `$fpath` for files starting with `_` and registers them as completion candidates. Run by oh-my-zsh once at startup.
12	2. **`$fpath`** is zsh's function search path. Order in this repo (`dot_zshrc.tmpl:67-70`):
13	   ```
14	   ~/.zfunc                                             ← user-generated (this repo's lazy autoload target)
15	   ~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/zsh-completions/src/     ← community (184 tools)
16	   ~/.docker/completions/                               ← Docker-shipped
17	   $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/site-functions/           ← Homebrew-managed
18	   ```
19	3. **The first line of each file** matters: `#compdef <name>` tells zsh which command to bind to. If you write `#compdef fleet`, then `fleet<TAB>` invokes the file's `_fleet` function.
20	4. **Autoload vs eager-load**: a file in `$fpath` is *parsed* the first time the user actually TABs the command (lazy). Files sourced explicitly at startup (e.g. via `load_modular_dir` in this repo) call `compdef _<func> <cmd>` directly — parsed eagerly, no need to be in `$fpath`.
21	5. **`_arguments` DSL** (zsh-only) lets you describe options + positional args declaratively: `'--hosts=[help text]:hosts:_fleet_hosts_csv'` defines the flag, hint, and a custom completer function. See `dot_config/zsh/tools/45_fleet_completion.zsh`.
22	
23	### bash — `bash-completion v2` + `complete -F` + `COMPREPLY`
24	
25	1. **bash-completion v2** is sourced at shell startup by `dot_config/bash/03_completion.bash`. It auto-loads completion files on first TAB.
26	2. **The user dir** is `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/bash-completion/completions/` — drop a file named after the command (e.g. `mi-router`) here and v2 lazy-loads it on TAB.
27	3. **`complete -F _func cmd`** registers a bash function as the completer for `cmd`. The function reads `$COMP_WORDS` / `$COMP_CWORD` and writes candidates to `$COMPREPLY`.
28	4. **`_init_completion` + `compgen`** are bash-completion v2 helpers — `_init_completion` populates `cur`/`prev`/`words`/`cword`; `compgen -W "list" -- "$cur"` filters a wordlist by the current prefix.
29	5. **Eager vs lazy** mirrors zsh: a file in the user dir is lazy; a file sourced via `load_modular_dir` (this repo's `dot_config/bash/`) calls `complete -F` immediately.
30	
31	### Three generation strategies in this repo
32	
33	| Strategy | Where the file lives | Trigger | Best for |
34	|---|---|---|---|
35	| **A. Lazy autoload** | zsh `~/.zfunc/_<tool>` / bash `${XDG_DATA_HOME}/bash-completion/completions/<tool>` | First TAB on the command | Tools that ship `--print-completion <shell>` or similar (tyro, click, clap-derive — including this repo's `mi-router`) |
36	| **B. Eager-load at startup** | `dot_config/zsh/tools/<NN>_<tool>_completion.zsh` + `dot_config/bash/<NN>_<tool>_completion.bash` | Sourced via `load_modular_dir` after compinit / bash-completion v2 init | Hand-written completion (this repo's `fleet`, `mlf`, `pqsum`, `x`) |
37	| **C. Cached eval at startup** | `${XDG_CACHE_HOME}/<shell>/<tool>_completion.<ext>` | Sourced via shell `init` script (`dot_config/shell/<NN>_<tool>.sh`) | Slow generators whose output has side effects beyond `compdef` (e.g. `thefuck --alias` outputs an `alias` line — needs to land in the running shell's namespace, not just a deferred `_<tool>` function) |
38	
39	Cache invalidation in classes A and C uses **binary-mtime check**:
40	```sh
41	[ ! -f "$cache" ] || [ "$(command -v <tool>)" -nt "$cache" ]  # → regenerate
42	```
43	This catches `brew upgrade`, `uv tool upgrade`, `mise install <NEW>` — anything that bumps the binary's mtime. Manual `<tool>-update-completion` helpers (in `dot_config/{shell,zsh}/10_aliases.zsh`) cover edge cases (gem-only upgrades, in-place replacements, cache corruption).
44	
45	## Architecture
46	
47	```
48	compinit runs once (inside oh-my-zsh.sh)
49	        │
50	        ├── ~/.zfunc/                          ← user-generated completions (NOT tracked by chezmoi)
51	        ├── ~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/       ← community completions (184 files, cloned by ansible)
52	        │     └── zsh-completions/src/
53	        ├── ~/.docker/completions/             ← Docker-shipped completions
54	        ├── $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/        ← Homebrew-managed completions (via `brew completions link`)
55	        │     └── site-functions/
56	        └── $ZSH/completions/                  ← oh-my-zsh built-in completions
57	```
58	
59	All `fpath` additions are in `dot_zshrc.tmpl` **before** `source "$ZSH/oh-my-zsh.sh"`, so `compinit` runs exactly once and picks up everything.
60	
61	## Completion Categories
62	
63	Tools fall into four categories:
64	
65	### A. Self-generating (`tool completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_tool`)
66	
67	Most modern CLI tools can output their own completion script. **Auto-generated for both shells** by the `chezmoi apply` hook (`run_after_50_generate_completions.sh.tmpl` → `scripts/generate_completions.sh`); see [Generating Completions After Fresh Install](#generating-completions-after-fresh-install) for opt-out + manual rerun.
68	
69	| Tool | Command |
70	|------|---------|
71	| `uv` | `uv generate-shell-completion zsh` |
72	| `mise` | `mise completion zsh` |
73	| `chezmoi` | `chezmoi completion zsh` |
74	| `just` | `just --completions zsh` |
75	| `bat` | `bat --completion zsh` |
76	| `delta` | `delta --generate-completion zsh` |
77	| `starship` | `starship completions zsh` |
78	| `rg` | `rg --generate complete-zsh` |
79	| `fd` | `fd --gen-completions zsh` |
80	| `zellij` | `zellij setup --generate-completion zsh` |
81	| `sesh` | `sesh completion zsh` |
82	| `pueue` | `pueue completions zsh` |
83	| `docker` | `docker completion zsh` |
84	| `gh` | `gh completion -s zsh` |
85	| `opencode` | `opencode completion zsh` |
86	| `bw` | `bw completion --shell zsh` |
87	
88	**Usage pattern:**
89	
90	```bash
91	# Generate once (or after upgrade)
92	mkdir -p ~/.zfunc
93	uv generate-shell-completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_uv
94	mise completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_mise
95	```
96	
97	### B. Pre-bundled (no action needed)
98	
99	Completions ship with the package or via the `zsh-completions` community plugin.
100	
101	| Tool | Source |
102	|------|--------|
103	| `eza` | Homebrew formula installs `_eza` into site-functions |
104	| `git` | oh-my-zsh `git` plugin |
105	| `yazi` | Ships `_yazi` in release assets (also in zsh-completions) |
106	| `lazygit` | No completion support; not needed (TUI app) |
107	| `btop` | No completion support; not needed (TUI app) |
108	| Many others | `zsh-completions` plugin covers 184 tools |
109	
110	### C. Eval/source at startup (shell integration)
111	
112	These tools inject completions as part of broader shell integration. Most live in the POSIX `dot_config/shell/` layer (sourced by both zsh and bash); zsh-only ones live in `dot_config/zsh/tools/`.
113	
114	| Tool | Where | How | Cached? |
115	|------|-------|-----|---------|
116	| `fzf` | `dot_config/shell/10_fzf.sh` | `eval "$(fzf --zsh)"` (zsh) / `eval "$(fzf --bash)"` (bash) | — |
117	| `zoxide` | `dot_config/shell/20_zoxide.sh` | `eval "$(zoxide init <shell>)"` | — |
118	| `direnv` | `dot_config/shell/30_direnv.sh` | `eval "$(direnv hook <shell>)"` | — |
119	| `marimo` | `dot_config/shell/29_marimo.sh` | `_MARIMO_COMPLETE=<shell>_source marimo` | ✅ `${XDG_CACHE_HOME}/{zsh,bash}/marimo_completion.{zsh,bash}` — refresh via `marimo-update-completion` |
120	| `thefuck` | `dot_config/shell/27_thefuck.sh` | `thefuck --alias` | ✅ `${XDG_CACHE_HOME}/{zsh,bash}/thefuck_alias.{zsh,bash}` — refresh via `thefuck-update-completion` |
121	| `try-cli` | `dot_config/zsh/tools/32_try.zsh` | `ruby try.rb init` (zsh-only) | ✅ `${XDG_CACHE_HOME}/zsh/try_init.zsh` — refresh via `try-update-completion` |
122	
123	> **Cached entries** auto-invalidate when the tool's binary mtime is newer than the cache file (`[ "$(command -v <tool>)" -nt "$cache" ]`) — catches `mise install <NEW>`, `brew upgrade`, `uv tool upgrade`. Manual refresh helpers handle edge cases: gem-only upgrades that don't bump the ruby binary, in-place tool replacements, or cache corruption. The pattern mirrors `dot_config/zsh/tools/95_bitwarden.zsh` (the canonical example).
124	
125	### D. No completion support
126	
127	`claude`, `gemini`, `agy`/`agyc` (Antigravity CLI), `btop`, `lazygit` -- no generation command available.
128	
129	### E. Python tools via `shtab` / `tyro` / `click` / `argcomplete`
130	
131	Python CLI frameworks can generate completions. Pick by what your script uses:
132	
133	- **[tyro](https://brentyi.github.io/tyro/tab_completion/)** (this repo's `mi-router` + every `scripts/fleet/*.py` and `scripts/mlf/*.py` subcommand): `<tool> --tyro-write-completion zsh <path>`. Native flag — auto-added when you call `tyro.cli(...)`. tyro emits `#compdef <full-binary-path>` for zsh, so post-process the first line to the short name (see `dot_config/shell/47_mi_router.sh` for the canonical pattern). Bash output already binds `basename`, no fixup needed.
134	- **[shtab](https://github.com/iterative/shtab)**: `shtab --shell=zsh my_module.parser > ~/.zfunc/_my_tool`. Decorate-an-`argparse.ArgumentParser` style; works for both shells.
135	- **argcomplete**: `register-python-argcomplete tool_name` (eval-at-startup style, category C). Requires the script to call `argcomplete.autocomplete(parser)` before `parse_args()`. Cross-shell.
136	- **click** (used by `marimo`, `thefuck`, `mlflow`, `litellm`, etc.): `_TOOL_COMPLETE=zsh_source tool > ~/.zfunc/_tool`. The completion script may include side effects (aliases / functions) — if so, treat as category C and cache via `${XDG_CACHE_HOME}/<shell>/<tool>_completion.<ext>`. See the canonical pattern at `dot_config/shell/29_marimo.sh`.
137	
138	> **TAB display itself**, not just completion data: see [`oh-my-zsh-plugins.md`](oh-my-zsh-plugins.md) "TAB display upgrades — alternatives evaluated" for fzf-tab (recommended) and rejected alternatives (zsh-autocomplete / carapace-bin / inshellisense).
139	
140	### F. In-house CLIs (this repo)
141	
142	| CLI | Source | Framework | Strategy | Files |
143	|---|---|---|---|---|
144	| `mi-router` | `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_mi-router` | tyro | A (lazy autoload) | `dot_config/shell/47_mi_router.sh` (gen + mtime check); refresh helper `mi-router-update-completion` |
145	| `reyee` | `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_reyee` | tyro | A (lazy autoload) | `dot_config/shell/48_reyee.sh` (gen + mtime check); refresh helper `reyee-update-completion` |
146	| `ping-monitor` | `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_ping-monitor` | bash hand-rolled | B | `dot_config/zsh/tools/50_ping_monitor_completion.zsh` + `dot_config/bash/50_ping_monitor_completion.bash` |
147	| `fleet` | `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_fleet` + `scripts/fleet/*.py` | hand-rolled umbrella + tyro/argparse subs | B (eager hand-written) | `dot_config/zsh/tools/45_fleet_completion.zsh` + `dot_config/bash/45_fleet_completion.bash` |
148	| `mlf` | `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_mlf` + `scripts/mlf/*.py` | hand-rolled umbrella + tyro subs | B | `dot_config/zsh/tools/46_mlf_completion.zsh` + `dot_config/bash/46_mlf_completion.bash` |
149	| `pqsum` | `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_pqsum` | argparse | B | `dot_config/zsh/tools/48_pqsum_completion.zsh` + `dot_config/bash/48_pqsum_completion.bash` |
150	| `x` | `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x` | bash hand-rolled | B | `dot_config/zsh/tools/49_x_completion.zsh` + `dot_config/bash/49_x_completion.bash` |
151	| `dotcfg` | `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_dotcfg` (thin shell → `scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py reconfigure`) | bash wrapper | B | `dot_config/zsh/tools/51_dotcfg_completion.zsh` + `dot_config/bash/51_dotcfg_completion.bash` (keys mirror PROMPTS) |
152	| `agent-warmup` | `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_agent-warmup` | argparse (subcommands) | B | `dot_config/zsh/tools/52_agent_warmup_completion.zsh` + `dot_config/bash/52_agent_warmup_completion.bash` |
153	| `aiblock` | `scripts/aiblock.py` | questionary (interactive TUI) | — (no CLI args) | (not needed) |
154	
155	**Dynamic candidates wired up:**
156	
157	- `fleet` host names — `_fleet_hosts_one` / `_fleet_hosts_csv` shell out to `fleet hosts --list`. Used for the positional `fleet hosts NAME`, `fleet chezmoi diff HOST`, `fleet chezmoi tail HOST`, and the `--hosts=foo,bar,baz` CSV flag everywhere.
158	- `pqsum -g <GROUP>` — `_pqsum` shells out to `pueue status --json | jq '.groups | keys[]'`.
159	- `mlf` ids (run-id, experiment-id, model-name) — **not** auto-completed (would round-trip MLflow tracking server, possibly auth-required). Use `tv mlflow` for fuzzy id picking instead.
160	
161	**Adding a new in-house CLI** (decision flow):
162	
163	1. **Does it use tyro?** → Use Strategy A. Mirror `dot_config/shell/47_mi_router.sh`. Add a `<tool>-update-completion` helper to `dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh`. Don't forget to rewrite `#compdef` in zsh post-gen.
164	2. **Does it use argparse?** → Two sub-options:
165	   - Add `argcomplete.autocomplete(parser)` to the script + Strategy C cached eval at startup.
166	   - Hand-write Strategy B completion (smaller / no Python dependency at every shell startup).
167	3. **Hand-rolled / shell script** → Strategy B hand-written. One zsh file in `dot_config/zsh/tools/<NN>_<name>_completion.zsh`, one bash file in `dot_config/bash/<NN>_<name>_completion.bash`. Mirror `_fleet`'s structure: top-level dispatcher → per-subcommand functions → dynamic helpers.
168	4. **Update this table + `docs/shells/aliases.md`** in the same commit (per the cross-file maintenance rule in `CLAUDE.md`).
169	
170	## Why `~/.zfunc/` is NOT Tracked by Chezmoi
171	
172	**Decision: `~/.zfunc/` is not version-controlled.** Rationale:
173	
174	1. **Completions are tool-version-dependent.** A completion script generated by `uv 0.6` may not match `uv 0.7`. Tracking stale files causes subtle breakage.
175	2. **Not all users install the same tools.** A `_pueue` completion file is useless (and throws warnings) if pueue isn't installed.
176	3. **Regeneration is trivial.** One command per tool.
177	4. **Brew-installed tools auto-manage their completions** via site-functions. Duplicating them in `~/.zfunc/` creates conflicts.
178	
179	### What we DO track
180	
181	- `fpath+=~/.zfunc` in `dot_zshrc.tmpl` (ensures the directory is in the search path)
182	- `zsh-completions` plugin cloned by ansible (community completions)
183	- `~/.docker/completions` fpath entry
184	- Tool-specific `eval`/`source` integrations in `dot_config/zsh/tools/`
185	
186	## Generating Completions After Fresh Install
187	
188	**Automatic — no manual step needed.** Every `chezmoi apply` runs `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_after_50_generate_completions.sh.tmpl`, which calls `scripts/generate_completions.sh` and regenerates completion for the 14 self-generating tools listed in Section A (`chezmoi`, `mise`, `uv`, `just`, `starship`, `gh`, `docker`, `rg`, `fd`, `bat`, `delta`, `zellij`, `pueue`, `opencode`).
189	
190	The hook is **idempotent** — it stat-checks each tool's binary mtime against the existing completion file and skips if the cache is fresh. Cost when nothing changed: **~21ms** total (presence checks + 28 stat calls). After an `ansible-playbook` / `brew upgrade` / `mise install <NEW>` that bumps a binary's mtime: ~140ms one-shot to regenerate the affected completions.
191	
192	Output paths:
193	- **zsh**: `~/.zfunc/_<tool>` — lazy-loaded by compinit on first TAB (in `$fpath` via `dot_zshrc.tmpl:68`).
194	- **bash**: `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/bash-completion/completions/<tool>` — lazy-loaded by bash-completion v2 on first TAB.
195	
196	### Manual rerun
197	
198	```bash
199	just completions-refresh                              # force regen all (--force)
200	bash scripts/generate_completions.sh --force          # same, no `just`
201	bash scripts/generate_completions.sh                  # mtime-checked (same as the chezmoi hook)
202	```
203	
204	Use `just completions-refresh` after a tool upgrade outside the chezmoi flow (e.g. `cargo install <tool>`), or to recover from a corrupted completion file.
205	
206	### Opt out
207	
208	```bash
209	export CHEZMOI_SKIP_COMPLETION_GEN=1   # in ~/.shellrc.adhoc; suppresses the chezmoi-apply hook
210	```
211	
212	Existing completion files stay as-is; you can still run `just completions-refresh` manually.
213	
214	### Add a new tool to the auto-gen inventory
215	
216	Edit the `regen <tool> "<zsh-args>" "<bash-args>"` block in `scripts/generate_completions.sh`. The arguments are whatever follows the tool name to produce the per-shell completion script — check `<tool> completion --help` or `<tool> --help | grep -i complet`. Examples already in the script cover click (`_TOOL_COMPLETE=`), clap (`--generate complete-<shell>`), tyro (`--tyro-write-completion <shell>`-equivalent), cobra (`completion <shell>`), and ad-hoc styles (`--completions <shell>`).
217	
218	### What about tools NOT in the auto-gen inventory?
219	
220	- **`sesh` / `tv` / `worktrunk`**: shell-startup mtime check (each tool has its own `dot_config/zsh/tools/<NN>_<tool>.zsh` file that runs the version check on every shell start — these tools are typically `cargo install`-ed outside chezmoi, so they need the per-startup probe to catch user upgrades).
221	- **`bw` / `marimo` / `thefuck` / `try-cli`**: cached eval at startup (their completion script has side effects beyond `compdef`, so the file is `source`'d into the running shell rather than autoloaded).
222	- **`mi-router`**: tyro self-gen, lives in `dot_config/shell/47_mi_router.sh` (not the bulk script — has its own `#compdef` rewrite for tyro's full-path output quirk).
223	- **`fleet` / `mlf` / `pqsum` / `x` / `dotcfg` / `agent-warmup`**: hand-written completion in `dot_config/{zsh/tools,bash}/45-52_*_completion.*` (in-house CLIs without a built-in completion generator). `dotcfg`'s `--set` key list mirrors the PROMPTS table in `scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py`.
224	
225	## Priority / Override Order
226	
227	When the same `_tool` file exists in multiple fpath directories, the **first match wins**:
228	
229	```
230	1. ~/.zfunc/                                    (highest - your overrides)
231	2. ~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/zsh-completions/src/
232	3. ~/.docker/completions/
233	4. $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/site-functions/   (Homebrew-managed)
234	5. /usr/share/zsh/*/functions/                  (system, lowest)
235	```
236	
237	Current `dot_zshrc.tmpl` order:
238	
239	```zsh
240	fpath+=~/.zfunc                     # appended (lowest of custom)
241	fpath=(zsh-completions/src $fpath)  # prepended (higher than ~/.zfunc)
242	fpath=(~/.docker/completions $fpath) # prepended (highest of custom)
243	```
244	
245	If you want `~/.zfunc/` to override community completions, change to prepend:
246	
247	```zsh
248	fpath=(~/.zfunc $fpath)  # prepend instead of append
249	```
250	
251	## FAQ
252	
253	**Q: Should I generate completions for tools that `zsh-completions` already covers?**
254	A: Only if you want the latest version. The community plugin may lag behind. For fast-moving tools (uv, mise), generating your own is worthwhile.
255	
256	**Q: A completion file throws errors after I uninstall a tool. What do I do?**
257	A: Remove the file: `rm ~/.zfunc/_toolname`. Stale `_tool` files in fpath are harmless (silently ignored) unless they have syntax errors.
258	
259	**Q: How do I debug completion issues?**
260	A: Run `echo $fpath | tr ' ' '\n'` to see all fpath entries. Use `which _toolname` to see which completion file is being used. Force rebuild with `rm -f ~/.zcompdump && compinit`.
261

```text
# 56_clipboard_history.sh — cross-platform clipboard-history helpers.
#
# Wraps Maccy (macOS, plaintext SQLite) and CopyQ (Linux, shipped CLI) behind
# a unified `cb` / `cbl` / `cbe` API. Replaces the Raycast-specific helper
# deleted in 2026-05 — Raycast 1.7+ encrypts its DB with SQLCipher and the
# key cannot be recovered without binary RE; see
# pitfalls/raycast-clipboard-sqlcipher-key-not-recoverable.md.
#
# Backend selection (override autodetect with CLIP_BACKEND=copyq|maccy):
#   macOS:  prefer Maccy SQLite, fall back to CopyQ if installed manually.
#   Linux:  CopyQ only.
# No backend → one-line install hint to stderr (ubuntu_server typical case).
#
# Maccy schema (verified against p0deje/Maccy@master HistoryItem.swift +
# HistoryItemContent.swift, 2026-05):
#   ZHISTORYITEM(Z_PK, ZAPPLICATION, ZFIRSTCOPIEDAT, ZLASTCOPIEDAT,
#                ZNUMBEROFCOPIES, ZPIN, ZTITLE)
#   ZHISTORYITEMCONTENT(Z_PK, ZTYPE, ZVALUE, ZITEM -> ZHISTORYITEM.Z_PK)
# Core Data dates are seconds since 2001-01-01; add 978307200 for Unix epoch.

# ---- backend detection -----------------------------------------------------

_clip_maccy_path() {
    p="$HOME/Library/Application Support/Maccy/Storage.sqlite"
    [ -f "$p" ] && { printf 'maccy:%s\n' "$p"; return 0; }
    p="$HOME/Library/Containers/org.p0deje.Maccy/Data/Library/Application Support/Maccy/Storage.sqlite"
    [ -f "$p" ] && { printf 'maccy:%s\n' "$p"; return 0; }
    return 1
}

_clip_copyq_ready() {
    command -v copyq >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
    copyq size >/dev/null 2>&1
}

_clip_backend() {
    case "${CLIP_BACKEND:-}" in
        copyq) _clip_copyq_ready && echo copyq ;;
        maccy) _clip_maccy_path ;;
        '')
```
</details></tool-use>

176	_PATH_PRELUDE = (
177	    "$HOME/.dotfiles/bin:$HOME/.cargo/bin:$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/bin:"
178	    "/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin:"
179	    "$HOME/.linuxbrew/bin:$PATH"
180	)
181	
182	
183	def _build_remote_cmd(argv: list[str], *, shell: str, login: bool, no_augment_path: bool) -> str:
184	    """Construct the shell string to send over SSH.
185	
186	    Decision matrix:
187	      shell="" + login=False + no_augment_path=False → PATH prelude + exec <quoted argv>
188	      shell="" + login=False + no_augment_path=True  → exec <quoted argv>
189	      shell=<bin> + login=False                       → PATH prelude + <bin> -c '<argv-joined>'
190	      shell="" + login=True                           → bash -lc '<quoted argv>'
191	      shell=<bin> + login=True                        → <bin> -lc '<argv-joined>'
192	
193	    In --shell modes the argv is joined with literal spaces (no shlex.quote)
194	    so users get shell-expansion as advertised. In non-shell modes each arg
195	    is shlex.quoted so the remote /bin/sh -c invocation (asyncssh always
196	    wraps in sh -c when run() gets a string) doesn't re-parse globs etc.
197	    """
198	    if shell:
199	        inner = " ".join(argv)
200	        shell_bin = shell
201	        flag = "-lc" if login else "-c"
202	        wrapped = f"{shell_bin} {flag} {shlex.quote(inner)}"
203	    elif login:
204	        inner = " ".join(shlex.quote(a) for a in argv)
205	        wrapped = f"bash -lc {shlex.quote(inner)}"
206	    else:
207	        wrapped = " ".join(shlex.quote(a) for a in argv)
208	
209	    # PATH prelude only when NOT login (login shells load PATH from rc files)
210	    # and NOT --no-augment-path.
211	    if not login and not no_augment_path:
212	        return f'export PATH="{_PATH_PRELUDE}"; {wrapped}'
213	    return wrapped
214

216	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
217	# Per-host execution
218	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
219	@dataclass
220	class HostResult:
221	    host: str
222	    rc: int | None  # None = SSH/timeout error
223	    stdout: str
224	    stderr: str
225	    elapsed_ms: int
226	    error: str | None = None  # SSH/timeout class name + message
227	
228	
229	async def _run_one(
230	    host: Host,
231	    argv: list[str],
232	    *,
233	    shell: str,
234	    login: bool,
235	    no_augment_path: bool,
236	    connect_timeout: float,
237	    cmd_timeout: float,
238	) -> HostResult:
239	    started = time.monotonic()
240	    cmd = _build_remote_cmd(argv, shell=shell, login=login, no_augment_path=no_augment_path)
241	    try:
242	        if host.local:
243	            proc = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
244	                "bash", "-c", cmd,
245	                stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
246	                stderr=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
247	            )
248	            try:
249	                stdout_b, stderr_b = await asyncio.wait_for(proc.communicate(), timeout=cmd_timeout)
250	            except asyncio.TimeoutError:
251	                proc.kill()
252	                raise TimeoutError(f"local cmd exceeded {cmd_timeout}s")
253	            rc = proc.returncode
254	            stdout = stdout_b.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
255	            stderr = stderr_b.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
256	        else:
257	            connect_kw = _connect_kwargs(host)
258	            async with asyncio.timeout(connect_timeout):
259	                conn = await asyncssh.connect(**connect_kw)
260	            try:
261	                async with asyncio.timeout(cmd_timeout):
262	                    result = await conn.run(cmd, check=False)
263	                rc = result.exit_status
264	                stdout = (result.stdout or "") if isinstance(result.stdout, str) else (result.stdout or b"").decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
265	                stderr = (result.stderr or "") if isinstance(result.stderr, str) else (result.stderr or b"").decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
266	            finally:
267	                conn.close()
268	                await conn.wait_closed()
269	        return HostResult(
270	            host=host.name,
271	            rc=rc if rc is not None else 0,
272	            stdout=stdout,
273	            stderr=stderr,
274	            elapsed_ms=int((time.monotonic() - started) * 1000),
275	        )
276	    except (asyncssh.Error, OSError, asyncio.TimeoutError, TimeoutError) as e:
277	        return HostResult(
278	            host=host.name,
279	            rc=None,
280	            stdout="",
281	            stderr="",
282	            error=f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}",
283	            elapsed_ms=int((time.monotonic() - started) * 1000),
284	        )
285	
286	
287	async def discover_exec(
288	    hosts: list[Host],
289	    argv: list[str],
290	    *,
291	    shell: str,
292	    login: bool,
293	    no_augment_path: bool,
294	    parallelism: int = 8,
295	    serial: bool = False,
296	    connect_timeout: float = 15.0,
297	    cmd_timeout: float = 60.0,
298	) -> list[HostResult]:
299	    parallelism = 1 if serial else max(1, parallelism)
300	    sem = asyncio.Semaphore(parallelism)
301	    done_count = 0
302	
303	    async def _bounded(h: Host) -> HostResult:
304	        nonlocal done_count
305	        async with sem:
306	            try:
307	                return await _run_one(
308	                    h, argv,
309	                    shell=shell, login=login, no_augment_path=no_augment_path,
310	                    connect_timeout=connect_timeout, cmd_timeout=cmd_timeout,
311	                )
312	            finally:
313	                done_count += 1
314	
315	    total = len(hosts)
316	
317	    async def _ticker(status: Any) -> None:
318	        while True:
319	            status.update(f"executing on {done_count}/{total} hosts...")
320	            await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
321	
322	    if err.is_terminal:
323	        with err.status(f"executing on {total} hosts...", spinner="dots") as status:
324	            tick = asyncio.create_task(_ticker(status))
325	            try:
326	                return list(await asyncio.gather(*(_bounded(h) for h in hosts)))
327	            finally:
328	                tick.cancel()
329	    return list(await asyncio.gather(*(_bounded(h) for h in hosts)))
330

335	def _first_line(s: str, fallback: str = "—") -> str:
336	    if not s:
337	        return fallback
338	    return s.splitlines()[0] if s.splitlines() else s.strip() or fallback

341	def render_table(results: list[HostResult], argv: list[str], full_output: bool, console: Console) -> None:
342	    title = f"fleet exec — {' '.join(shlex.quote(a) for a in argv)}"
343	    table = Table(title=title, header_style="bold cyan")
344	    table.add_column("HOST", style="bold")
345	    table.add_column("RC", justify="right")
346	    table.add_column("STDOUT (1L)" if not full_output else "STDOUT/STDERR")
347	    table.add_column("ms", justify="right", style="dim")
348	
349	    for r in results:
350	        if r.rc is None:
351	            table.add_row(r.host, "[red]N/A[/red]", f"[red]{(r.error or '')[:80]}[/red]", str(r.elapsed_ms))
352	            continue
353	        rc_cell = f"[green]{r.rc}[/green]" if r.rc == 0 else f"[red]{r.rc}[/red]"
354	        body = _first_line(r.stdout) if r.rc == 0 else _first_line(r.stderr, fallback=_first_line(r.stdout))
355	        table.add_row(r.host, rc_cell, body, str(r.elapsed_ms))
356	    console.print(table)
357	
358	    if full_output:
359	        for r in results:
360	            console.print()
361	            header = Text()
362	            header.append(f"── {r.host} ──", style="bold cyan")
363	            console.print(header)
364	            if r.error:
365	                console.print(Text(r.error, style="red"))
366	                continue
367	            if r.stdout:
368	                console.print(Text("[stdout]", style="bold dim"))
369	                console.print(r.stdout.rstrip())
370	            if r.stderr:
371	                console.print(Text("[stderr]", style="bold red"))
372	                console.print(r.stderr.rstrip())

379	def write_out_dir(results: list[HostResult], out_dir: str, argv: list[str]) -> None:
380	    base = Path(out_dir)
381	    base.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
382	    for r in results:
383	        safe_host = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9._-]", "_", r.host)
384	        (base / f"{safe_host}.stdout").write_text(r.stdout, encoding="utf-8")
385	        (base / f"{safe_host}.stderr").write_text(r.stderr, encoding="utf-8")
386	        (base / f"{safe_host}.json").write_text(json.dumps({
387	            "host": r.host,
388	            "rc": r.rc,
389	            "elapsed_ms": r.elapsed_ms,
390	            "error": r.error,
391	            "argv": argv,
392	        }, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
393	    err.print(f"[dim]fleet exec: wrote {len(results)} hosts × 3 files to {out_dir}[/dim]")

396	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
397	# AI: agent dispatch + cache + prompt + render
398	# (Copy-pasted from dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_pqsum. 4th consumer of the
399	# AICAP SSOT — extraction is the next priority.)
400	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
401	def detect_agent() -> str | None:
402	    if AICAP_AGENT:
403	        if AICAP_AGENT == "http" or shutil.which(AICAP_AGENT):
404	            return AICAP_AGENT
405	        err.print(f"[red]AICAP_AGENT={AICAP_AGENT!r} but that CLI isn't on PATH.[/red]")
406	        return None
407	    for cand in AICAP_AGENT_PRIORITY:
408	        if shutil.which(cand):
409	            return cand
410	    return None
411	
412	
413	def model_for(agent: str) -> str:
414	    return {
415	        "claude": AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL or "(default)",
416	        "opencode": AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL or "(default)",
417	        "codex": AICAP_CODEX_MODEL or "(default)",
418	        "agyc": "(account)",
419	        "cursor-agent": AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL or "(default)",
420	        "http": AICAP_HTTP_MODEL,
421	    }.get(agent, "?")
422	
423	
424	def invoke_agent(agent: str, prompt: str, timeout: float) -> str:
425	    if agent == "http":
426	        return _invoke_http(prompt, timeout)
427	    base = AGENT_CONFIG[agent]["base"]
428	    try:
429	        result = subprocess.run([*base, prompt], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
430	    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
431	        err.print(f"[red]{agent} timed out after {timeout:.0f}s[/red]")
432	        return ""
433	    except FileNotFoundError:
434	        err.print(f"[red]{agent} not on PATH (race vs detect_agent)[/red]")
435	        return ""
436	    if result.returncode != 0:
437	        err.print(f"[red]{agent} exited {result.returncode}[/red]")
438	        if result.stderr.strip():
439	            err.print(f"[dim]{result.stderr.strip()[:500]}[/dim]")
440	        return ""
441	    return result.stdout
442	
443	
444	def _invoke_http(prompt: str, timeout: float) -> str:
445	    payload = json.dumps({
446	        "model": AICAP_HTTP_MODEL,
447	        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
448	        "stream": False,
449	    }).encode("utf-8")
450	    headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json"}
451	    if AICAP_HTTP_API_KEY:
452	        headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {AICAP_HTTP_API_KEY}"
453	    req = urllib.request.Request(AICAP_HTTP_URL, data=payload, headers=headers, method="POST")
454	    try:
455	        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as resp:
456	            body = resp.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
457	    except (urllib.error.HTTPError, urllib.error.URLError, TimeoutError) as e:
458	        err.print(f"[red]http: {e}[/red]")
459	        return ""
460	    try:
461	        parsed = json.loads(body)
462	        return parsed["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]
463	    except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError, IndexError, TypeError):
464	        err.print(f"[red]http: unexpected response shape[/red] [dim]{body[:300]}[/dim]")
465	        return ""
466	
467	
468	_CACHE_VERSION = "v1"
469	_AI_OUTPUT_CAP = 4000  # per-host stdout/stderr cap when building the prompt
470	
471	
472	def _cache_path(prompt_hash: str) -> Path:
473	    base = os.environ.get("XDG_CACHE_HOME") or os.path.expanduser("~/.cache")
474	    d = Path(base) / "fleet-exec"
475	    d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
476	    host = socket.gethostname().split(".")[0] or "host"
477	    return d / f"{host}-{prompt_hash}.json"
478	
479	
480	def _cache_lookup(prompt_hash: str) -> dict | None:
481	    p = _cache_path(prompt_hash)
482	    if not p.is_file():
483	        return None
484	    try:
485	        data = json.loads(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
486	    except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError):
487	        return None
488	    if data.get("version") != _CACHE_VERSION:
489	        return None
490	    if data.get("prompt_hash") != prompt_hash:
491	        return None
492	    age = time.time() - float(data.get("generated_at", 0))
493	    parsed = data.get("parsed")
494	    if not isinstance(parsed, dict):
495	        return None
496	    if age > FLEETEXEC_MIN_REFRESH_INTERVAL > 0:
497	        return None
498	    return parsed
499	
500	
501	def _cache_save(prompt_hash: str, parsed: dict) -> None:
502	    p = _cache_path(prompt_hash)
503	    try:
504	        p.write_text(json.dumps({
505	            "version": _CACHE_VERSION,
506	            "prompt_hash": prompt_hash,
507	            "generated_at": time.time(),
508	            "parsed": parsed,
509	        }, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
510	    except OSError as e:
511	        err.print(f"[yellow]fleet exec: cache write failed: {e}[/yellow]")
512	
513	
514	def _truncate_for_ai(s: str) -> str:
515	    if len(s) <= _AI_OUTPUT_CAP:
516	        return s
517	    return s[:_AI_OUTPUT_CAP] + f"\n[... {len(s) - _AI_OUTPUT_CAP} more chars truncated ...]"
518	
519	
520	def build_ai_prompt(results: list[HostResult], argv: list[str]) -> str:
521	    # NOTE: elapsed_ms is intentionally NOT in this payload — it varies every
522	    # run and would bust the cache key on every invocation. The LLM classifies
523	    # based on stdout/stderr/rc, which are the stable signals.
524	    payload = {
525	        "command": " ".join(shlex.quote(a) for a in argv),
526	        "hosts": [
527	            {
528	                "host": r.host,
529	                "rc": r.rc,
530	                "error": r.error,
531	                "stdout": _truncate_for_ai(r.stdout),
532	                "stderr": _truncate_for_ai(r.stderr),
533	            }
534	            for r in results
535	        ],
536	    }
537	    return AIEXEC_PROMPT_PREAMBLE + "\n--- INPUT ---\n" + json.dumps(payload, indent=2, default=str) + "\nReturn JSON now.\n"
538	
539	
540	_TIERS = ("succeeded", "differed", "failed")
541	
542	
543	def parse_reply(reply: str) -> dict | None:
544	    if not reply.strip():
545	        return None
546	    s = reply.strip()
547	    if s.startswith("```"):
548	        s = s.split("\n", 1)[1] if "\n" in s else s
549	        if s.endswith("```"):
550	            s = s.rsplit("```", 1)[0]
551	        s = s.strip()
552	    start, end = s.find("{"), s.rfind("}")
553	    if start == -1 or end == -1 or end < start:
554	        return None
555	    try:
556	        parsed = json.loads(s[start:end + 1])
557	    except json.JSONDecodeError:
558	        return None
559	    if not isinstance(parsed, dict) or not isinstance(parsed.get("hosts"), list):
560	        return None
561	
562	    cleaned_hosts: list[dict] = []
563	    for h in parsed["hosts"]:
564	        if not isinstance(h, dict):
565	            continue
566	        tier = str(h.get("tier", "")).strip().lower()
567	        if tier not in _TIERS:
568	            tier = "failed"
569	        rc_raw = h.get("rc")
570	        try:
571	            rc = int(rc_raw) if rc_raw is not None else None
572	        except (TypeError, ValueError):
573	            rc = None
574	        elapsed_raw = h.get("elapsed_ms")
575	        try:
576	            elapsed = int(elapsed_raw) if elapsed_raw is not None else 0
577	        except (TypeError, ValueError):
578	            elapsed = 0
579	        cleaned_hosts.append({
580	            "host": str(h.get("host", "")).strip()[:80],
581	            "tier": tier,
582	            "summary": str(h.get("summary", "")).strip()[:200],
583	            "rc": rc,
584	            "elapsed_ms": elapsed,
585	        })
586	    return {
587	        "command": str(parsed.get("command", "")).strip()[:400],
588	        "majority_output": str(parsed.get("majority_output", "")).strip()[:400],
589	        "hosts": cleaned_hosts,
590	        "fleet_summary": str(parsed.get("fleet_summary", "")).strip()[:400],
591	    }
592	
593	
594	def invoke_ai(results: list[HostResult], argv: list[str], *, refresh: bool, no_cache: bool, dry_run: bool) -> dict | None:
595	    prompt = build_ai_prompt(results, argv)
596	    if dry_run:
597	        print(prompt)
598	        return None
599	    prompt_hash = hashlib.sha256(prompt.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]
600	    if not refresh and not no_cache:
601	        cached = _cache_lookup(prompt_hash)
602	        if cached is not None:
603	            return cached
604	    agent = detect_agent()
605	    if agent is None:
606	        tried = ", ".join(AICAP_AGENT_PRIORITY)
607	        err.print(f"[red]No coding-agent CLI on PATH (tried: {tried}).[/red]")
608	        err.print("[dim]Install one, or set AICAP_AGENT=http with AICAP_HTTP_API_KEY.[/dim]")
609	        return None
610	    with err.status(f"[dim]{agent} ({model_for(agent)}) thinking…[/dim]", spinner="dots"):
611	        reply = invoke_agent(agent, prompt, FLEETEXEC_TIMEOUT)
612	    parsed = parse_reply(reply)
613	    if parsed is None:
614	        err.print("[yellow]fleet exec: LLM returned no parseable JSON[/yellow]")
615	        if reply.strip():
616	            err.print(f"[dim]{reply.strip()[:400]}[/dim]")
617	        return None
618	    if not no_cache:
619	        _cache_save(prompt_hash, parsed)
620	    return parsed
621	
622	
623	_TIER_GLYPHS = {"succeeded": "🟢", "differed": "🟡", "failed": "🔴"}
624	_TIER_COLORS = {"succeeded": "green", "differed": "yellow", "failed": "red"}
625	
626	
627	def render_ai(parsed: dict, console: Console) -> None:
628	    fleet = parsed.get("fleet_summary") or ""
629	    if fleet:
630	        console.print(Text(f"🌐 {fleet}", style="bold cyan"))
631	        console.print()
632	    majority = parsed.get("majority_output") or ""
633	    if majority:
634	        console.print(Text(f"majority: {majority}", style="dim italic"))
635	        console.print()
636	    # Group by tier for readability
637	    by_tier: dict[str, list[dict]] = {t: [] for t in _TIERS}
638	    for h in parsed.get("hosts", []):
639	        by_tier.setdefault(h.get("tier", "failed"), []).append(h)
640	    for tier in _TIERS:
641	        hosts = by_tier.get(tier, [])
642	        if not hosts:
643	            continue
644	        glyph = _TIER_GLYPHS.get(tier, "⚪")
645	        color = _TIER_COLORS.get(tier, "white")
646	        console.print(Text(f"{glyph} {tier} ({len(hosts)})", style=f"bold {color}"))
647	        for h in hosts:
648	            line = Text()
649	            line.append("  ")
650	            line.append(f"{h.get('host', '?'):<16}", style="bold")
651	            rc = h.get("rc")
652	            rc_str = "N/A" if rc is None else str(rc)
653	            line.append(f"rc={rc_str:<4}", style="dim")
654	            line.append(f"  {h.get('summary', '')}", style="white")
655	            console.print(line)
656	        console.print()
657	
658	
659	def render_ai_report(parsed: dict, results: list[HostResult], argv: list[str]) -> str:
660	    lines: list[str] = []
661	    ts = datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
662	    cmd_str = " ".join(shlex.quote(a) for a in argv)
663	    lines.append(f"# fleet exec report — {ts}")
664	    lines.append("")
665	    lines.append(f"**Command:** `{cmd_str}`")
666	    lines.append("")
667	    fleet = parsed.get("fleet_summary") or ""
668	    if fleet:
669	        lines.append(f"**Fleet:** {fleet}")
670	        lines.append("")
671	    majority = parsed.get("majority_output") or ""
672	    if majority:
673	        lines.append(f"**Majority output:** {majority}")
674	        lines.append("")
675	
676	    by_tier: dict[str, list[dict]] = {t: [] for t in _TIERS}
677	    for h in parsed.get("hosts", []):
678	        by_tier.setdefault(h.get("tier", "failed"), []).append(h)
679	    for tier in _TIERS:
680	        hosts = by_tier.get(tier, [])
681	        if not hosts:
682	            continue
683	        lines.append(f"## {tier.title()} ({len(hosts)})")
684	        lines.append("")
685	        for h in hosts:
686	            rc = h.get("rc")
687	            rc_str = "N/A" if rc is None else str(rc)
688	            lines.append(f"- **{h.get('host', '?')}** (rc={rc_str}, {h.get('elapsed_ms', 0)}ms) — {h.get('summary', '')}")
689	        lines.append("")
690	
691	    lines.append("## Raw outputs")
692	    lines.append("")
693	    lines.append("<details>")
694	    lines.append("<summary>per-host stdout/stderr</summary>")
695	    lines.append("")
696	    for r in results:
697	        lines.append(f"### {r.host}")
698	        lines.append("")
699	        lines.append(f"rc={r.rc if r.rc is not None else 'N/A'}  elapsed={r.elapsed_ms}ms")
700	        lines.append("")
701	        if r.error:
702	            lines.append(f"**Error:** `{r.error}`")
703	            lines.append("")
704	            continue
705	        if r.stdout.strip():
706	            lines.append("```")
707	            lines.append(r.stdout.rstrip())
708	            lines.append("```")
709	            lines.append("")
710	        if r.stderr.strip():
711	            lines.append("stderr:")
712	            lines.append("```")
713	            lines.append(r.stderr.rstrip())
714	            lines.append("```")
715	            lines.append("")
716	    lines.append("</details>")
717	    lines.append("")
718	    return "\n".join(lines)

720	
721	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
722	# CLI
723	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
724	def _filter_hosts(hosts: list[Host], include: str | None, exclude: str | None) -> list[Host]:
725	    if include:
726	        wanted = {h.strip() for h in include.split(",") if h.strip()}
727	        hosts = [h for h in hosts if h.name in wanted]
728	    if exclude:
729	        unwanted = {h.strip() for h in exclude.split(",") if h.strip()}
730	        hosts = [h for h in hosts if h.name not in unwanted]
731	    return hosts
732	
733	
734	def parse_args(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> argparse.Namespace:
735	    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(
736	        prog="fleet exec",
737	        description="Run an ad-hoc command across the fleet (argv list after `--`).",
738	        usage="fleet exec [OPTIONS] -- COMMAND [ARG...]",
739	    )
740	    p.add_argument("--hosts", default=None, help="Comma-separated host names to include")
741	    p.add_argument("--exclude", default=None, help="Comma-separated host names to exclude")
742	    p.add_argument("--config", default=str(DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH), help="Path to machines.toml")
743	    p.add_argument("--shell", default="", help="Wrap command in `<SHELL> -c` (e.g. bash, zsh, sh). Default off.")
744	    p.add_argument("--login", action="store_true", help="Wrap in `-lc` so the host's rc files load (slower).")
745	    p.add_argument("--no-augment-path", action="store_true",
746	                   help="Skip the standard PATH prelude (default: ~/.dotfiles/bin → cargo → uv → ~/bin → brew). Mutually exclusive with --login.")
747	    p.add_argument("--json", dest="json_out", action="store_true", help="Emit per-host JSON to stdout.")
748	    p.add_argument("--out-dir", default="", help="Write per-host .stdout/.stderr/.json files under DIR.")
749	    p.add_argument("--full-output", action="store_true", help="Render full stdout/stderr blocks below the table.")
750	    p.add_argument("--ai", action="store_true", help="Summarize results into succeeded/differed/failed tiers via the configured LLM.")
751	    p.add_argument("--report", action="store_true", help="With --ai: emit markdown report.")
752	    p.add_argument("--out", default="", help="With --ai --report: write to PATH (default stdout).")
753	    p.add_argument("--refresh", action="store_true", help="With --ai: bypass cache.")
754	    p.add_argument("--no-cache", action="store_true", help="With --ai: don't read or write the cache.")
755	    p.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true", help="With --ai: print prompt; no LLM call.")
756	    p.add_argument("--serial", action="store_true", help="Process hosts one at a time (debug).")
757	    p.add_argument("--max-parallel", type=int, default=0, help="Max concurrent SSH connections (default min(8, len(hosts))).")
758	    p.add_argument("--connect-timeout", type=float, default=15.0, help="Per-host SSH connect timeout (seconds).")
759	    p.add_argument("--command-timeout", type=float, default=60.0, help="Per-host remote command timeout (seconds).")
760	    p.add_argument("argv", nargs=argparse.REMAINDER, help="Command + args after `--`.")
761	    return p.parse_args(argv)
762	
763	
764	def main() -> int:
765	    args = parse_args(sys.argv[1:])
766	
767	    # Strip leading `--` if present (argparse.REMAINDER keeps it).
768	    inner_argv = list(args.argv)
769	    if inner_argv and inner_argv[0] == "--":
770	        inner_argv = inner_argv[1:]
771	    if not inner_argv:
772	        err.print("[red]fleet exec: missing command after `--`[/red]")
773	        err.print("[dim]Usage: fleet exec [OPTIONS] -- COMMAND [ARG...][/dim]")
774	        return 2
775	
776	    if args.no_augment_path and args.login:
777	        err.print("[red]fleet exec: --no-augment-path and --login are mutually exclusive[/red]")
778	        err.print("[dim]Login shells load PATH from rc files; augmentation is redundant.[/dim]")
779	        return 2
780	
781	    if args.ai and args.out_dir:
782	        err.print("[yellow]fleet exec: --ai overrides --out-dir; AI output mode used[/yellow]")
783	
784	    try:
785	        all_hosts, _defaults = load_hosts(Path(args.config))
786	    except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError) as e:
787	        err.print(f"[red]error loading {args.config}: {e}[/red]")
788	        return 2
789	
790	    selected = _filter_hosts(all_hosts, args.hosts, args.exclude)
791	    if not selected:
792	        err.print("[yellow]no hosts matched filter[/yellow]")
793	        return 0
794	
795	    parallelism = 1 if args.serial else (args.max_parallel or min(8, len(selected)))
796	    results = asyncio.run(discover_exec(
797	        selected, inner_argv,
798	        shell=args.shell, login=args.login, no_augment_path=args.no_augment_path,
799	        parallelism=parallelism, serial=args.serial,
800	        connect_timeout=args.connect_timeout, cmd_timeout=args.command_timeout,
801	    ))
802	
803	    if args.ai:
804	        parsed = invoke_ai(results, inner_argv,
805	                           refresh=args.refresh, no_cache=args.no_cache, dry_run=args.dry_run)
806	        if args.dry_run:
807	            return 0
808	        if parsed is None:
809	            return 1
810	        if args.report or args.out:
811	            report = render_ai_report(parsed, results, inner_argv)
812	            if args.out:
813	                try:
814	                    Path(args.out).write_text(report, encoding="utf-8")
815	                    err.print(f"[dim]fleet exec: wrote {args.out}[/dim]")
816	                except OSError as e:
817	                    err.print(f"[red]fleet exec: failed to write {args.out}: {e}[/red]")
818	                    return 1
819	            else:
820	                print(report)
821	        else:
822	            render_ai(parsed, Console())
823	    elif args.json_out:
824	        emit_json(results)
825	    else:
826	        render_table(results, inner_argv, full_output=args.full_output, console=Console())
827	        if args.out_dir:
828	            write_out_dir(results, args.out_dir, inner_argv)
829	
830	    failed = sum(1 for r in results if r.rc is None or r.rc != 0)
831	    return min(failed, 125)
832	
833	
834	if __name__ == "__main__":
835	    sys.exit(main())

54	## Quick Setup
55	
56	### Interactive (recommended)
57	
58	```bash
59	curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/main/bootstrap.sh | bash
60	```
61	
62	Installs [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) (if missing) and launches `dotfiles-init` — a Python wrapper that groups the ~19 chezmoi prompts into a clean multi-select UI, offers pre-set bundles (`personal-mac` / `work-mac` / `server-linux` / `cloud-vm` / `minimal`), checks SSH keys, then calls real `chezmoi init` with your answers pre-filled. Full docs: [`scripts/init/README.md`](scripts/init/README.md).
63	
64	On first-run or slow networks the `uv` resolver can sit silently for a few minutes — use the verbose form to see timestamped progress + `uv --verbose` resolver output + `set -x`:
65	
66	```bash
67	curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/main/bootstrap.sh | DOTFILES_BOOTSTRAP_VERBOSE=1 bash
68	```
69	
70	Pass extra args through to the wrapper via `bash -s --` (e.g. run the schema-parity checker instead of the default `init`):
71	
72	```bash
73	curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/main/bootstrap.sh | bash -s -- doctor
74	```
75	
76	Behind GFW? Set `DOTFILES_RAW_URL` / `DOTFILES_REF` to point at a mirror, or use the non-interactive path below.
77	
78	### Non-interactive (direct chezmoi)
79	
80	```bash
81	# Installs chezmoi to ~/.local/bin and walks through the raw prompts one-by-one.
82	# Uses HTTPS to avoid SSH key setup on fresh machines.
83	export GITHUB_USERNAME=daviddwlee84
84	sh -c "$(curl -fsLS get.chezmoi.io)" -- -b "$HOME/.local/bin" init --apply "https://github.com/$GITHUB_USERNAME/dotfiles.git"
85	
86	# After install, switch the chezmoi source repo to SSH (so future `chezmoi update` uses your SSH key):
87	#   chezmoi cd
88	#   git remote set-url origin git@github.com:$GITHUB_USERNAME/dotfiles.git
89	#   exit
90	```
91	
92	This automatically:
93	
94	1. Bootstraps Homebrew (macOS/Linux), uv, mise, ansible
95	2. Deploys all config files
96	3. Runs ansible playbooks (git, ripgrep, fd, neovim, etc.)
97	4. Runs brew bundle (if `installBrewApps` is enabled, or on macOS if `installAiDesktopApps` / `installGamingApps` is enabled)
98	
99	#### Sudo password injection (when chezmoi can't open `/dev/tty`)
100	
101	Some Linux environments — notably **CentOS 7 + AD/LDAP user with high UID** where `pam_systemd` never created `/run/user/<UID>/` — leave the chezmoi-spawned bootstrap script unable to open `/dev/tty`, so the shared sudo helper can't prompt and Linuxbrew aborts with `Insufficient permissions to install Homebrew to "/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew"`. The fix is to pre-stage the password via `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` (the same env-var [`fleet_apply`](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md) uses over SSH).
102	
103	The repo ships [`scripts/apply_with_sudo.sh`](scripts/apply_with_sudo.sh) to handle the prompt → 0600 tmpfile → export → run → `shred` dance:
104	
105	```bash
106	# First time (chezmoi not installed yet):
107	sh -c "$(curl -fsLS get.chezmoi.io)" -- -b "$HOME/.local/bin"   # install chezmoi only
108	bash <(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/$GITHUB_USERNAME/dotfiles/main/scripts/apply_with_sudo.sh) \
109	  --init "https://github.com/$GITHUB_USERNAME/dotfiles.git"
110	
111	# Re-runs (after chezmoi source is cloned at ~/.local/share/chezmoi):
112	just apply-with-sudo                                              # interactive prompt
113	just apply-with-sudo --pass-from-env                              # reads $SUDO_PASSWORD
114	SUDO_PASSWORD=xxx just apply-with-sudo --pass-from-env            # one-liner
115	```
116	
117	The wrapper validates the password against `sudo -v` before invoking `chezmoi`, then shreds the tmpfile on exit (any signal). Inside chezmoi's run-scripts, `sudo_session_init` adopts the file, moves it into the shared state dir, and spawns the watchdog that keeps the sudo timestamp warm.
118	
119	**Even simpler alternative** if you have root and don't mind editing sudoers: add `$USER ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL` to `/etc/sudoers.d/99-bootstrap`, run `chezmoi apply`, then remove the line. The shared helper short-circuits cleanly when sudo is truly passwordless.
120	
121	> CentOS 7 also blocks Linuxbrew install because system curl 7.29 is older than Homebrew's 7.41 minimum, and Homebrew bottles built on Ubuntu 22.04+ don't run on glibc 2.17 anyway. Linuxbrew is fully optional on Linux — every ansible task that uses it has a non-brew fallback (cargo / GitHub musl release / AppImage). On CentOS 7, drop a stub `~/.local/bin/brew` (`#!/bin/sh\nexit 0`) before applying to short-circuit the bootstrap's brew step.
122	
123	Full diagnosis: [`pitfalls/bootstrap-no-tty-sudo-prompt-skipped.md`](pitfalls/bootstrap-no-tty-sudo-prompt-skipped.md) and [`pitfalls/centos7-noroot.md`](pitfalls/centos7-noroot.md).
124	
125	### After install
126	
127	- `~/.local/bin` and the rest of the shared layer (mise/uv/cargo/bun PATH, plus Linux OpenCode's `~/.opencode/bin`) are exported via `~/.config/shell/00_exports.sh`, sourced by both the chezmoi-managed `~/.bashrc` and `~/.zshrc`.
128	- On sudo-enabled machines, the ansible role for your `primaryShell` choice switches your login shell automatically (`zsh` role for `primaryShell=zsh`, `bash` role for `primaryShell=bash`). Log out / back in to pick it up, or run `exec zsh` / `exec bash` now.
129	- `primaryShell=bash` on macOS additionally installs Homebrew bash 5.x and adds it to `/etc/shells` (system bash 3.2 is too old for oh-my-bash plugins + ble.sh). zsh-primary mac users see no extra brew install.
130	- On `noRoot=true` installs, login shell isn't changed — run `exec zsh` / `exec bash` per session, or ask your sysadmin: `sudo chsh -s "$(command -v zsh)" $USER` (or `bash`).
131	- Open a new shell after install so PATH changes take effect. Both `~/.bashrc` and `~/.zshrc` are deployed regardless of `primaryShell` choice, so the other shell still works ad-hoc.
132
