181	## What You Get
182	
183	### Config Files
184	
185	- `~/.gitconfig` - Git configuration; managed via `modify_` so `gh auth setup-git`'s `[credential "..."]` blocks (with the per-machine absolute path to `gh`) survive `chezmoi apply` ([docs](docs/tools/gh-cli.md))
186	- `~/.config/git/hooks/` - Global Git hooks (via a global `core.hooksPath`): managed `pre-commit` (gitleaks) + Git LFS hooks, all hardened to skip gracefully — PATH-robust and non-fatal so a stripped-PATH clone like `brew tap` can't break (see [pitfall](pitfalls/git-lfs-global-hook-breaks-brew-tap.md))
187	- `~/.config/gh-dash/config.yml` - Global gh-dash config, with `diffnav` as the diff pager
188	- `~/.config/lazygit/config.yml` - Global LazyGit config, with `delta` as the custom diff pager
189	- `~/.config/bat/themes/tokyonight_night.tmTheme` - Managed Tokyo Night theme for bat; apply rebuilds the bat cache and clears it if the cache is incompatible with `delta`
190	- `~/.config/nvim/` - Neovim (LazyVim) configuration; system clipboard via `unnamedplus`, with an SSH-conditional OSC 52 override so remote yanks reach the local clipboard (pairs with tmux `set-clipboard on`, see [docs](docs/tools/tmux/README.md#osc-52-clipboard-ssh-friendly-yank))
191	- `~/.config/uv/uv.toml` - uv package manager config (PyPI: official / Aliyun+TUNA+USTC via `useChineseMirror`)
192	- `~/.cargo/config.toml` - Cargo registry config (crates.io / TUNA sparse index via `useChineseMirror`)
193	- `~/.npmrc` - npm registry config (official/npmmirror via `useChineseMirror`)
194	- `~/.config/.bunfig.toml` - Bun global registry config (official/npmmirror via `useChineseMirror`)
195	- `~/.gemrc` - RubyGems source + common options (TUNA mirror; only managed when `useChineseMirror=true`, gated via `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`)
196	- `~/.condarc` - Conda/Mamba channels with TUNA Anaconda mirror (only managed when `useChineseMirror=true`, preserves `auto_activate_base`/user channel prefs)
197	- `~/.config/zsh/00_exports.zsh` - Env-var mirror bundle (Homebrew / Rustup / mise / GOPROXY) when `useChineseMirror=true`; also exported by bootstrap + ansible runner scripts so first-run installs and ansible subprocesses inherit them ([docs](docs/tools/mirrors.md))
198	- `~/.config/zsh/99_local_proxy.zsh` - Create-only machine-local proxy override stub; uncomment `LOCAL_PROXY_URL` / `LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL` here to pin Clash ports without future chezmoi diffs
199	- `~/.docker/config.json` - Docker client `proxies.default` block (auto-injected from `$LOCAL_PROXY_URL` / `$LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL`; preserves `auths` / `credsStore` via chezmoi modify-script) ([docs](docs/tools/containers.md))
200	- `~/.config/docker/daemon.json` - Rootless Docker `registry-mirrors` (DaoCloud / USTC / NJU / ...; Linux + `useChineseMirror` only) ([docs](docs/tools/containers.md#strategy-a-registry-mirrors-in-daemonjson))
201	- `~/.config/alacritty/` - Alacritty terminal config (CSI-u keybindings for `Ctrl+Number` tmux window switching, `option_as_alt` for Meta keys)
202	- `~/Library/Application Support/{Code,Cursor,Antigravity}/User/` (macOS) + `~/.config/{Code,Cursor,Antigravity}/User/` (Linux) - Editor settings overlay: `modify_settings.json` deep-merges a 6-key baseline (Hack Nerd Font Mono, relative line numbers, format on save, smart-accept suggestion, terminal font) into each editor's live `settings.json` without overwriting other keys; `create_keybindings.json` seeds 5 universal keybindings on a fresh machine and never overwrites editor-added entries. Canonical templates live under [`.chezmoitemplates/editor/`](.chezmoitemplates/editor/); `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` gates each editor dir with a `stat` presence check so uninstalled editors never produce phantom directories.
203	- `~/.config/ghostty/config` - Ghostty/cmux terminal config (`macos-option-as-alt` for tmux Meta keybindings, disabled ligatures, explicit `clipboard-write = allow` / `clipboard-read = ask` for OSC 52) ([docs](docs/tools/ghostty.md))
204	- `~/.config/starship.toml` - Starship cross-shell prompt config
205	- `~/.xonshrc` + `~/.config/xonsh/rc.xsh` - Optional [Xonsh](https://xon.sh/) (Python-superset shell) startup + extension sandbox. Installed via `python_uv_tools` with a curated set of xontribs (`jedi`/`zoxide`/`pipeliner`/`fzf-widgets`); **not** a login shell — drop in with `xonsh` for ad-hoc Python-in-shell work ([docs](docs/shells/xonsh.md))
206	- `~/.config/direnv/direnvrc` - direnv helper functions, including `.venv`-aware Python activation
207	- `~/.config/yazi/` - Yazi file manager config (v0.3.3+ syntax, [docs](https://yazi-rs.github.io/docs/configuration/overview/))
208	  - `yazi.toml` - Main config with open rules and openers (`o`/`O`)
209	  - `keymap.toml`, `theme.toml` - Optional customization files (stubs provided)
210	- `~/.config/btop/btop.conf` + `~/.config/btop/themes/catppuccin_mocha.theme` - btop system-monitor baseline (Catppuccin Mocha theme, process tree view, `vim_keys` mirrors `enableVimMode`); seeded once via `create_` so btop's on-exit config rewrites never cause chezmoi drift; catppuccin theme vendored like bat's ([docs](docs/tools/btop.md))
211	- `~/.claude/` - Claude Code settings
212	- `~/.cursor/cli-config.json`, `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`, `~/.codex/config.toml` - Coding-agent CLI overlays: each `modify_*` script deep-merges a small managed baseline (preferences, features, curated plugins) into the CLI's live config, preserving auth tokens, per-project trust, sessions, and other machine-local state. Codex specifically round-trips `[projects]` and `[marketplaces.*]` so per-project trust paths never get clobbered. OpenCode legacy `~/.config/opencode/config.json` is migrated to the modern filename by a one-shot `run_once_before_50_opencode_migrate.sh.tmpl`. Full design: [docs/tools/agent-overlays.md](docs/tools/agent-overlays.md).

214	- `~/.tmux.conf` - Tmux configuration with TPM plugins (resurrect, continuum, tmux-floax floating pane, tmux-fzf for fuzzy keybinding/session/pane search rebound to `prefix+?`, tmux-fzf-url, tmux-open), vim-style copy mode with clipboard yank, capture-pane helpers (`prefix+y`/`Y`/`C-y`), a native popup menu (`prefix+Space` or `prefix+e`, script-driven with submenus and height-aware trimming) with layout/resize/session management, popup shell (`prefix+\``) and lazygit popup (`prefix+G`), a glow-rendered cheatsheet (`prefix+Space` → `?`), vim-style pane nav, `Ctrl+1..9` quick window switching (CSI-u terminals), extended-keys for coding agents (including `Ctrl+/` in Neovim), sesh keybindings (`prefix+g` fzf picker, `prefix+T` television picker, `prefix+O` built-in picker, `prefix+W` window picker, `prefix+S` last), responsive Catppuccin status bar (adapts modules to terminal width for mobile), and config reload on `prefix+R` ([docs](docs/tools/tmux/README.md))
215	- `~/.dotfiles/bin/x` - Cross-platform terminal wrapper for `copy` / `copy-file` / `paste` / `open`; `x copy` has an OSC 52 fallback for SSH text copy, while `x copy-file` copies desktop file objects for Finder / Files paste ([docs](docs/tools/clipboard.md))
216	- `~/.dotfiles/bin/sms` - Huawei router SMS reader (HiLink XML API; verification-code extraction, clipboard integration, TV channel) ([docs](docs/tools/sms.md))

455	      ansible.builtin.file:
456	        path: "{{ item }}"
457	        state: absent
458	      loop:
459	        - /tmp/trippy.tar.gz
460	        - /tmp/trippy-user

581	# --- rustscan (fast port scanner) ---
582	- name: Check if rustscan is installed
583	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]
584	  ansible.builtin.command: rustscan --version
585	  register: rustscan_check
586	  changed_when: false
587	  failed_when: false
588	
589	- name: Install rustscan from GitHub releases (Debian/Ubuntu)
590	  when:
591	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]
592	    - rustscan_check.rc != 0
593	  block:
594	    - name: Ensure ~/.local/bin exists (rustscan)
595	      ansible.builtin.file:
596	        path: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin"
597	        state: directory
598	        mode: '0755'
599	
600	    - name: Set rustscan arch mapping
601	      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
602	        rustscan_arch: >-
603	          {{
604	            'x86_64' if target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64']
605	            else 'aarch64' if target_architecture in ['aarch64', 'arm64']
606	            else target_architecture
607	          }}
608	
609	    - name: Download rustscan archive (x86_64)
610	      when: rustscan_arch == 'x86_64'
611	      ansible.builtin.get_url:
612	        url: "https://github.com/RustScan/RustScan/releases/latest/download/x86_64-linux-rustscan.tar.gz.zip"
613	        dest: /tmp/rustscan.zip
614	        mode: '0644'
615	        timeout: 120
616	      retries: 3
617	      delay: 5
618	
619	    - name: Download rustscan archive (aarch64)
620	      when: rustscan_arch == 'aarch64'
621	      ansible.builtin.get_url:
622	        url: "https://github.com/RustScan/RustScan/releases/latest/download/aarch64-linux-rustscan.zip"
623	        dest: /tmp/rustscan.zip
624	        mode: '0644'
625	        timeout: 120
626	      retries: 3
627	      delay: 5
628	
629	    - name: Extract and install rustscan (x86_64 - double wrapped)
630	      when: rustscan_arch == 'x86_64'
631	      ansible.builtin.shell: |
632	        set -e
633	        cd /tmp
634	        python3 -m zipfile -e rustscan.zip .
635	        tar xzf x86_64-linux-rustscan.tar.gz
636	        cp rustscan "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/rustscan"
637	        chmod 0755 "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/rustscan"
638	      args:
639	        executable: /bin/bash
640	      changed_when: true
641	
642	    - name: Extract and install rustscan (aarch64)
643	      when: rustscan_arch == 'aarch64'
644	      ansible.builtin.shell: |
645	        set -e
646	        cd /tmp
647	        python3 -m zipfile -e rustscan.zip .
648	        cp rustscan "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/rustscan"
649	        chmod 0755 "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/rustscan"
650	      args:
651	        executable: /bin/bash
652	      changed_when: true
653	
654	    - name: Clean up rustscan temp files
655	      ansible.builtin.shell: |
656	        rm -f /tmp/rustscan.zip /tmp/rustscan /tmp/x86_64-linux-rustscan.tar.gz /tmp/aarch64-linux-rustscan
657	      args:
658	        executable: /bin/bash
659	      changed_when: false
660	  rescue:
661	    - name: Warn rustscan installation failed
662	      ansible.builtin.debug:
663	        msg: "rustscan installation failed — skipping. Error: {{ ansible_failed_result.msg | default('unknown') }}"
664	
665	    - name: Clean up rustscan temp files (rescue)
666	      ansible.builtin.shell: |
667	        rm -f /tmp/rustscan.zip /tmp/rustscan /tmp/x86_64-linux-rustscan.tar.gz /tmp/aarch64-linux-rustscan
668	      args:
669	        executable: /bin/bash
670	      changed_when: false

672	# =============================================================================
673	# Tunnel tools — ngrok + cloudflared
674	# Tags: tunnel_tools (gated by installTunnelTools chezmoi flag)
675	# =============================================================================
676	
677	# --- ngrok ---
678	
679	- name: Install ngrok (macOS)
680	  tags: [tunnel_tools]
681	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
682	  block:
683	    # Skip the install when the binary is already on PATH — ngrok cask downloads
684	    # from bin.ngrok.com which periodically returns HTTP 52 "empty reply from
685	    # server" (Heroku-fronted, transient). Pre-checking lets re-applies short-
686	    # circuit instead of paying a 1-2 min download attempt that may fail.
687	    - name: Check if ngrok is already installed (macOS)
688	      ansible.builtin.command: which ngrok
689	      register: ngrok_present_macos
690	      changed_when: false
691	      failed_when: false
692	
693	    - name: Install ngrok via Homebrew (with retries for flaky bin.ngrok.com CDN)
694	      when: ngrok_present_macos.rc != 0
695	      community.general.homebrew:
696	        name: ngrok
697	        state: present
698	      register: ngrok_brew_install
699	      until: ngrok_brew_install is succeeded
700	      retries: 3
701	      delay: 15
702	
703	  rescue:
704	    # Most common failure: `Download failed: ... curl: (52) Empty reply from
705	    # server` from bin.ngrok.com (Heroku CDN). Transient — retrying minutes
706	    # later usually works. We don't fail the whole apply over it; user can
707	    # re-run `chezmoi apply --tag tunnel_tools` or `brew install --cask ngrok`
708	    # later. See pitfalls/ngrok-cask-download-flaky.md for the full story.
709	    - name: Warn ngrok installation failed (macOS)
710	      ansible.builtin.debug:
711	        msg: |-
712	          ngrok macOS installation failed after 3 retries — skipping. Re-run
713	          `brew install --cask ngrok` later. Error: {{ ansible_failed_result.msg | default('unknown') }}
714	
715	- name: Install ngrok (Debian/Ubuntu)
716	  tags: [tunnel_tools]
717	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
718	  block:
719	    - name: Check if ngrok is installed
720	      ansible.builtin.command: ngrok version
721	      register: ngrok_check
722	      changed_when: false
723	      failed_when: false
724	
725	    - name: Install ngrok via official apt repo (Debian/Ubuntu)
726	      when: ngrok_check.rc != 0
727	      become: true
728	      tags: [sudo]
729	      block:
730	        - name: Download ngrok apt GPG key
731	          ansible.builtin.get_url:
732	            url: https://ngrok-agent.s3.amazonaws.com/ngrok.asc
733	            dest: /tmp/ngrok.asc
734	            timeout: 60
735	
736	        - name: Install ngrok GPG key
737	          ansible.builtin.shell: |
738	            gpg --dearmor < /tmp/ngrok.asc > /etc/apt/keyrings/ngrok.gpg
739	            chmod 0644 /etc/apt/keyrings/ngrok.gpg
740	          args:
741	            creates: /etc/apt/keyrings/ngrok.gpg
742	
743	        - name: Add ngrok apt source
744	          ansible.builtin.copy:
745	            content: "deb [signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/ngrok.gpg] https://ngrok-agent.s3.amazonaws.com buster main\n"
746	            dest: /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ngrok.list
747	            mode: '0644'
748	
749	        - name: Install ngrok from apt
750	          ansible.builtin.apt:
751	            name: ngrok
752	            update_cache: true
753	            state: present
754	
755	    - name: Re-check ngrok after apt install
756	      ansible.builtin.command: ngrok version
757	      register: ngrok_recheck
758	      changed_when: false
759	      failed_when: false
760	
761	    - name: Install ngrok from tgz (user-level fallback)
762	      when: ngrok_recheck.rc != 0
763	      block:
764	        - name: Set ngrok tgz architecture
765	          ansible.builtin.set_fact:
766	            ngrok_tgz_arch: >-
767	              {{ 'amd64' if target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64']
768	                 else 'arm64' if target_architecture in ['aarch64', 'arm64']
769	                 else '' }}
770	
771	        - name: Ensure ~/.local/bin exists
772	          ansible.builtin.file:
773	            path: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin"
774	            state: directory
775	            mode: '0755'
776	
777	        - name: Download ngrok tgz (user-level)
778	          ansible.builtin.get_url:
779	            url: "https://bin.equinox.io/c/bNyj1mQVY4c/ngrok-v3-stable-linux-{{ ngrok_tgz_arch }}.tgz"
780	            dest: /tmp/ngrok.tgz
781	            timeout: 120
782	          when: ngrok_tgz_arch != ''
783	
784	        - name: Extract and install ngrok (user-level)
785	          ansible.builtin.shell: |
786	            set -e
787	            tar -xzf /tmp/ngrok.tgz -C /tmp/
788	            install -m 0755 /tmp/ngrok "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/ngrok"
789	          args:
790	            executable: /bin/bash
791	            creates: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/ngrok"
792	          changed_when: true
793	
794	        - name: Clean up ngrok tgz
795	          ansible.builtin.file:
796	            path: /tmp/ngrok.tgz
797	            state: absent
798	
799	  rescue:
800	    - name: Warn ngrok installation failed
801	      ansible.builtin.debug:
802	        msg: "ngrok installation failed — skipping. Error: {{ ansible_failed_result.msg | default('unknown') }}"
803	
804	    - name: Clean up ngrok temp files (rescue)
805	      ansible.builtin.file:
806	        path: "{{ item }}"
807	        state: absent
808	      loop:
809	        - /tmp/ngrok.tgz
810	        - /tmp/ngrok
811	        - /tmp/ngrok.asc
812	
813	- name: Install ngrok (RedHat/CentOS — tgz user-level)
814	  tags: [tunnel_tools]
815	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "RedHat"
816	  block:
817	    - name: Check if ngrok is installed (RedHat)
818	      ansible.builtin.command: ngrok version
819	      register: ngrok_rh_check
820	      changed_when: false
821	      failed_when: false
822	
823	    - name: Set ngrok tgz architecture (RedHat)
824	      when: ngrok_rh_check.rc != 0
825	      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
826	        ngrok_rh_arch: >-
827	          {{ 'amd64' if target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64']
828	             else 'arm64' if target_architecture in ['aarch64', 'arm64']
829	             else '' }}
830	
831	    - name: Ensure ~/.local/bin exists (RedHat)
832	      when: ngrok_rh_check.rc != 0 and ngrok_rh_arch | default('') != ''
833	      ansible.builtin.file:
834	        path: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin"
835	        state: directory
836	        mode: '0755'
837	
838	    - name: Download and install ngrok tgz (RedHat)
839	      when: ngrok_rh_check.rc != 0 and ngrok_rh_arch | default('') != ''
840	      ansible.builtin.shell: |
841	        set -e
842	        curl -fsSL "https://bin.equinox.io/c/bNyj1mQVY4c/ngrok-v3-stable-linux-{{ ngrok_rh_arch }}.tgz" -o /tmp/ngrok.tgz
843	        tar -xzf /tmp/ngrok.tgz -C /tmp/
844	        install -m 0755 /tmp/ngrok "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/ngrok"
845	        rm -f /tmp/ngrok.tgz /tmp/ngrok
846	      args:
847	        executable: /bin/bash
848	        creates: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/ngrok"
849	      changed_when: true
850	
851	  rescue:
852	    - name: Warn ngrok installation failed (RedHat)
853	      ansible.builtin.debug:
854	        msg: "ngrok installation failed on RedHat — skipping."
855	
856	    - name: Clean up ngrok temp files (RedHat rescue)
857	      ansible.builtin.shell: rm -f /tmp/ngrok.tgz /tmp/ngrok
858	      args:
859	        executable: /bin/bash
860	      changed_when: false

862	# --- cloudflared ---
863	
864	- name: Install cloudflared (macOS)
865	  tags: [tunnel_tools]
866	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
867	  community.general.homebrew:
868	    name: cloudflared
869	    state: present
870	
871	- name: Install cloudflared (Debian/Ubuntu)
872	  tags: [tunnel_tools]
873	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
874	  block:
875	    - name: Check if cloudflared is installed
876	      ansible.builtin.command: cloudflared version
877	      register: cf_check
878	      changed_when: false
879	      failed_when: false
880	
881	    - name: Set cloudflared deb architecture
882	      when: cf_check.rc != 0
883	      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
884	        cf_deb_arch: >-
885	          {{ 'amd64' if target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64']
886	             else 'arm64' if target_architecture in ['aarch64', 'arm64']
887	             else 'arm' if target_architecture in ['armv7l', 'armhf']
888	             else '' }}
889	
890	    - name: Install cloudflared .deb (system-level)
891	      when: cf_check.rc != 0 and cf_deb_arch | default('') != ''
892	      become: true
893	      tags: [sudo]
894	      block:
895	        - name: Get latest cloudflared release info
896	          ansible.builtin.uri:
897	            url: https://api.github.com/repos/cloudflare/cloudflared/releases/latest
898	            return_content: true
899	            timeout: 30
900	          register: cf_release
901	          retries: 3
902	          delay: 5
903	          until: cf_release is succeeded
904	
905	        - name: Download cloudflared .deb
906	          ansible.builtin.get_url:
907	            url: "https://github.com/cloudflare/cloudflared/releases/download/{{ cf_release.json.tag_name }}/cloudflared-linux-{{ cf_deb_arch }}.deb"
908	            dest: /tmp/cloudflared.deb
909	            timeout: 120
910	
911	        - name: Install cloudflared .deb
912	          ansible.builtin.apt:
913	            deb: /tmp/cloudflared.deb
914	            state: present
915	
916	        - name: Clean up cloudflared .deb
917	          ansible.builtin.file:
918	            path: /tmp/cloudflared.deb
919	            state: absent
920	
921	    - name: Re-check cloudflared after deb install
922	      ansible.builtin.command: cloudflared version
923	      register: cf_recheck
924	      changed_when: false
925	      failed_when: false
926	
927	    - name: Install cloudflared binary (user-level fallback)
928	      when: cf_recheck.rc != 0 and cf_deb_arch | default('') != ''
929	      block:
930	        - name: Ensure ~/.local/bin exists
931	          ansible.builtin.file:
932	            path: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin"
933	            state: directory
934	            mode: '0755'
935	
936	        - name: Get latest cloudflared release info (fallback)
937	          ansible.builtin.uri:
938	            url: https://api.github.com/repos/cloudflare/cloudflared/releases/latest
939	            return_content: true
940	            timeout: 30
941	          register: cf_release_fb
942	          retries: 3
943	          delay: 5
944	          until: cf_release_fb is succeeded
945	
946	        - name: Download cloudflared binary (user-level)
947	          ansible.builtin.get_url:
948	            url: "https://github.com/cloudflare/cloudflared/releases/download/{{ cf_release_fb.json.tag_name }}/cloudflared-linux-{{ cf_deb_arch }}"
949	            dest: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/cloudflared"
950	            mode: '0755'
951	            timeout: 120
952	
953	  rescue:
954	    - name: Warn cloudflared installation failed
955	      ansible.builtin.debug:
956	        msg: "cloudflared installation failed — skipping. Error: {{ ansible_failed_result.msg | default('unknown') }}"
957	
958	    - name: Clean up cloudflared temp files (rescue)
959	      ansible.builtin.file:
960	        path: /tmp/cloudflared.deb
961	        state: absent
962	
963	- name: Install cloudflared (RedHat/CentOS — rpm)
964	  tags: [tunnel_tools]
965	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "RedHat"
966	  block:
967	    - name: Check if cloudflared is installed (RedHat)
968	      ansible.builtin.command: cloudflared version
969	      register: cf_rh_check
970	      changed_when: false
971	      failed_when: false
972	
973	    - name: Set cloudflared rpm architecture (RedHat)
974	      when: cf_rh_check.rc != 0
975	      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
976	        cf_rpm_arch: >-
977	          {{ 'x86_64' if target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64']
978	             else 'aarch64' if target_architecture in ['aarch64', 'arm64']
979	             else '' }}
980	
981	    - name: Get latest cloudflared release info (RedHat)
982	      when: cf_rh_check.rc != 0 and cf_rpm_arch | default('') != ''
983	      ansible.builtin.uri:
984	        url: https://api.github.com/repos/cloudflare/cloudflared/releases/latest
985	        return_content: true
986	        timeout: 30
987	      register: cf_rh_release
988	      retries: 3
989	      delay: 5
990	      until: cf_rh_release is succeeded
991	
992	    - name: Install cloudflared .rpm (system-level)
993	      when: cf_rh_check.rc != 0 and cf_rpm_arch | default('') != ''
994	      become: true
995	      tags: [sudo]
996	      block:
997	        - name: Download cloudflared .rpm
998	          ansible.builtin.get_url:
999	            url: "https://github.com/cloudflare/cloudflared/releases/download/{{ cf_rh_release.json.tag_name }}/cloudflared-linux-{{ cf_rpm_arch }}.rpm"
1000	            dest: /tmp/cloudflared.rpm
1001	            timeout: 120
1002	
1003	        - name: Install cloudflared .rpm
1004	          ansible.builtin.shell: |
1005	            rpm -i --force /tmp/cloudflared.rpm
1006	          args:
1007	            executable: /bin/bash
1008	          changed_when: true
1009

214	
215	    # Single-key setup: the `InRelease` file is signed by the key at
216	    # packages.opentofu.org/.../gpgkey (subkey 70DF59811A8B9109). The old
217	    # dual-key approach also included get.opentofu.org/opentofu.gpg, but that
218	    # is an unrelated OpenTofu project key that does NOT sign the repo —
219	    # carrying it in signed-by= bought nothing. `deb-src` is dropped because
220	    # this Cloudsmith-style repo has no source packages and apt-get update
221	    # fails on the missing Sources file.
222	    # Dearmor the key to a temp file on the SAME dir, verify it is non-empty,
223	    # then atomically mv it into place. A cut-off download (flaky proxy / GFW)
224	    # otherwise leaves a 0-byte /etc/apt/keyrings/opentofu.gpg; since the .list
225	    # references it via signed-by=, every later apt-get update on the whole
226	    # machine then dies with NO_PUBKEY 70DF59811A8B9109 and wedges unrelated
227	    # roles. Never truncate the live keyring on a failed download. The refresh
228	    # is scoped to this one source so a sibling flaky repo cannot fail it.
229	    # See pitfalls/apt-update-fails-base-role-empty-error.md.
230	    - name: Install OpenTofu repo and package
231	      ansible.builtin.shell: |
232	        set -eo pipefail
233	        tmpkey=/etc/apt/keyrings/opentofu.gpg.tmp
234	        rm -f "$tmpkey"
235	        curl -fsSL https://packages.opentofu.org/opentofu/tofu/gpgkey | gpg --no-tty --batch --yes --dearmor -o "$tmpkey"
236	        test -s "$tmpkey"
237	        mv -f "$tmpkey" /etc/apt/keyrings/opentofu.gpg
238	        rm -f /etc/apt/keyrings/opentofu-repo.gpg
239	        echo "deb [signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/opentofu.gpg] https://packages.opentofu.org/opentofu/tofu/any/ any main" > /etc/apt/sources.list.d/opentofu.list
240	        apt-get update -o Dir::Etc::sourcelist=sources.list.d/opentofu.list -o Dir::Etc::sourceparts=- -o APT::Get::List-Cleanup=0
241	        apt-get install -y tofu
242	      args:
243	        executable: /bin/bash
244	      changed_when: true
245	  rescue:

247	      ansible.builtin.debug:

`grep -A 5 -B 5 "audio\|volume\|media" /Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/backlog/linux-desktop-app-control.md 2>/dev/null | head -40`

```text
| `apprunning NAME` | `pgrep -f <pattern>` | ✓ silent boolean |
| `appquit NAME` | `pkill -TERM -f <pattern>` | ✓ Electron + Firefox honour SIGTERM as graceful quit |
| `apprestart NAME` | quit + poll-gone (≤15s) + launch (launches even if not running) | ✓ |
| `appactivate NAME` | D-Bus → `org.gnome.Shell.Extensions.Windows.Activate(<wm-class>)` if `window-calls` ext present; else `applaunch` fallback | ⚠ true focus needs extension; degrades gracefully |
| `applist [--pids\|--all]` | registry + `.desktop` scan with absolute-Exec filter, pgrep each | ⚠ "managed apps that are alive" — not every window |
| `appresponsive NAME [T]` | `timeout T playerctl -p <mpris> status` for media apps; degrades to `apprunning` + stderr note otherwise | ⚠ MPRIS-only; no Linux analog to Apple Events |

**Override file** (`~/.config/shell/linux-apps.conf`, not auto-stubbed): `linux_app_register NAME --desktop=ID --pkill=REGEX --wm-class=CLASS [--mpris=NAME]`. Required for AppImage / Snap / Flatpak apps; recommended where multiple `.desktop` entries exist for one app. See the playbook for the user's 5-app starter snippet.

**tv channel** (`dot_config/television/cable/linux-apps.toml.tmpl`, gated on linux + `ubuntu_desktop`): mirrors `tv mac-apps` keybindings. Drops Alt+H (no Linux "hide windows" without compositor IPC).

```text
## Cross-file maintenance rules

When you touch one of these surfaces, update the listed mirror in the same commit.

| Surface you change | Also update | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| Config files / ansible roles / platforms / setup steps | `README.md` (What You Get, Supported Platforms, Quick Setup) | — |
| New `docs/**/*.md` | Nav entry in `mkdocs.yml`; run `uv run mkdocs build --strict` | known anchor-drift is tracked in [`backlog/mkdocs-anchor-drift.md`](backlog/mkdocs-anchor-drift.md) — don't tighten `validation.links.not_found` until cleared |
| New tool installed by an ansible role / Brewfile / curl-installer / mise / uv / npm / cargo / gem / dotnet (or removed, or switched mechanism) | Add / update / remove the row in [`docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md`](docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md) § Tool index (A–Z). If it's a new install **mechanism** (vs new tool through an existing mechanism), also update the relevant § Per-manager catalog subsection and § Decision tree | High-churn case is just the A–Z row (one line per tool). The doc is the install-side companion to [`docs/this_repo/upgrades.md`](docs/this_repo/upgrades.md) — if the new tool has a non-trivial upgrade story, update upgrades.md too. Reverse refs from both pages auto-link back. |

**Repo-root files that stay OUT of MkDocs nav** (`README.md`, `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` / `GEMINI.md`, `TODO.md`, `backlog/`, `pitfalls/`, `NOTES.md`): referenced via absolute GitHub URLs from [`docs/for-maintainers.md`](docs/for-maintainers.md), never copied via `pymdownx.snippets`.

**Three-tier file placement** for new shell helpers:

| Tier | Dir | When |
|---|---|---|
| Shared | `dot_config/shell/` | POSIX subset, both shells source. `$ZSH_VERSION`/`$BASH_VERSION` source-time dispatch is OK; ZLE widgets / `compdef` / `bindkey` / `setopt` / `read -q` / `${m:t}` / glob qualifiers are NOT (bash would error on source). |
| Zsh-only | `dot_config/zsh/` | ZLE widgets, `compdef`, `bindkey`, `setopt`, zsh-vi-mode hooks. |
| Bash-only | `dot_config/bash/` | `bind -x` / `ble-bind`, OMB plugin arrays, bash-specific `shopt`s. |

When porting a zsh-only helper to bash via ble.sh, extract the shell-agnostic backend into `dot_config/shell/` and keep each shell's widget binding in its own dir.

### Workmux status icon integration spans 6 files

Touching the `🤖`/`💬`/`✅` per-tmux-window status mechanism requires keeping these 6 surfaces in sync (full story: [docs/tools/workmux.md](docs/tools/workmux.md); pitfall: [pitfalls/workmux-status-leak.md](pitfalls/workmux-status-leak.md)):

1. `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` — binary install (brew tap on macOS; GitHub release `.tar.gz` on Linux)
2. `dot_config/workmux/config.yaml` — `status_format: false` is load-bearing
3. `dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf` — `#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}` appended to `@catppuccin_window_text` and `@catppuccin_window_current_text`
4. `dot_claude/modify_settings.json` — `Stop`/`SubagentStop`/`UserPromptSubmit`/`Notification` hooks calling `workmux set-window-status` (hook-aware merger preserves CodeIsland entries)
5. `dot_config/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts` + `dot_config/opencode/modify_package.json`
6. `dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh` — generic POSIX `tmux_status_set/get/clear/clear_all/list/run` for non-agent producers

**Hard rules**: never run `workmux setup` on a managed machine (would write parallel hook entries); never flip `status_format: true` (fights catppuccin's window-text override); never drop the `command -v workmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && … || true` guard in Claude hooks (spams errors on fresh boxes); never drop explicit `set-window-status done` from `Stop`/`SubagentStop` (upstream only ever sets `working`, never clears — that's the by-design leak documented in the pitfall). `wt` (worktrunk, `37_worktrunk.zsh`) and `wm` (workmux, `38_workmux.zsh`) stay distinct — different config formats, killer features, helper files.

### 3. **`fleet exec` — Shell Function Sourcing & PATH Prelude**

**Files involved:**
- `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/scripts/fleet/exec.py` (lines 176–180)
- `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_fleet` (lines 237–239)

**The `_PATH_PRELUDE` constant** (exec.py, lines 176–180):

```python
_PATH_PRELUDE = (
    "$HOME/.dotfiles/bin:$HOME/.cargo/bin:$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/bin:"
    "/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin:"
    "$HOME/.linuxbrew/bin:$PATH"
)
```

**How `fleet exec` runs commands:**

From the docstring (lines 1–20):
> 1. Default: argv list after `--`, **no shell expansion** (safe by construction).
> 2. `--shell <bin>` opt-in: wraps in `<bin> -c '<argv joined>'` so the user can use pipes / globs / redirects.
> 3. `--login` opt-in: wraps in `<shell> -lc '...'` so the remote rc files load (gives access to nvm / mise / conda / **aliases**).

**Decision matrix** (lines 183–213, `_build_remote_cmd` function):

```python
# Non-login, no shell → PATH prelude + exec <quoted argv>
# --shell bin (no login) → PATH prelude + <bin> -c '<argv-joined>'
# --shell bin + --login → <bin> -lc '<argv-joined>' (no PATH prelude, rc files load PATH)
# --login only → bash -lc <quoted argv> (no PATH prelude)
```

**Answer: Are sourced shell functions available to `fleet exec`?**

**It depends on the mode:**

1. **Default mode (`fleet exec -- CMD`):** NO. Only executables in `$PATH` are available. The remote shell is **non-interactive** and the user's rc files (where functions are sourced) are **not loaded**. Each arg is shlex-quoted, so pipes/globs won't expand either.

2. **With `--login` flag:** YES, if the function is in a standard rc file (`~/.bashrc`, `~/.zshrc`). The login shell loads all rc files, sourcing `dot_config/shell/*.sh` where your function would live.

3. **With `--shell bash` (no login):** NO by default. Shell expansion works (pipes, globs), but rc files aren't loaded. However, the `_PATH_PRELUDE` is still injected, so functions aren't available **unless they're already compiled into the shell binary or exported as aliases.**

**To use `fleet exec` with a shell function across hosts:**

```bash
# Option A: Use --login so rc files load
fleet exec --login -- sysmute toggle

# Option B: Inline the function definition (for non-interactive usage)
fleet exec -- sh -c 'sysmute_body() { ... }; sysmute_body toggle'

# Option C: Make it an executable in ~/.dotfiles/bin/ (symlink or wrapper)
# Then it appears in $PATH via the _PATH_PRELUDE
```

**PATH prelude details:**
- Order is intentional: **package managers win over ~/bin** (cargo → uv → brew order ensures reproducibility)
- **Deliberately diverges from interactive shell PATH** (which prioritizes ~/bin) to avoid legacy ~/bin shadowing modern tools
- Applied **only when NOT login** (login shells load PATH from rc files, so augmentation is redundant)

**mac-apps.toml.tmpl** (Lines 38-128):
```toml
[metadata]
name = "mac-apps"
description = "macOS apps — graceful quit / restart / activate / hide via Apple Events"

[source]
command = """osascript -e 'tell application "System Events"' ..."""
display = "{split:\\t:0}  {split:\\t:1}"
output = "{split:\\t:1}"  # App NAME by default for piping

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:activate"
alt-q = ["actions:quit", "reload_source"]
alt-r = ["actions:restart", "reload_source"]
alt-h = "actions:hide"
alt-k = ["actions:force-kill", "reload_source"]
alt-i = "actions:info"
alt-p = "actions:probe"

[preview]
command = [
  # Cycle 1: ps + lsappinfo
  # Cycle 2: responsiveness probe (slower)
]

[actions.activate]
description = "Bring app to front (Alt+Tab equivalent)"
command = """. ~/.config/shell/54_macos_apps.sh && appactivate '{split:\\t:1}'"""
mode = "fork"
```

**linux-apps.toml.tmpl** (Lines 41-126):
- Gated on: `{{- if and (eq .chezmoi.os "linux") (eq .profile "ubuntu_desktop") -}}`
- Mirrors mac-apps keybindings where applicable
- Drops `alt-h` (macOS-only; Linux can't hide windows without compositor)
- Uses `applist --pids` from the shell helper

**Key Pattern:**
- `[keybindings]`: Alt+ keys rather than Ctrl+ (tmux root-table shadows Ctrl+)
- `reload_source` action: reloads the app list after destructive operations (quit, restart, force-kill)
- Both `mode = "fork"` (async) and `mode = "execute"` (sync for polling)

### 8. macOS Implementation Patterns (AppleScript)

**Volume control via osascript:**
```bash
osascript \
    -e 'on run argv' \
    -e 'set vol to (item 1 of argv) as integer' \
    -e 'set volume output volume vol' \
    -e 'end run' \
    -- "$1"
```

**Mute status check:**
```bash
osascript -e 'output muted of (get volume settings)'
```

**Now-playing via System Events:**
```bash
osascript -e 'tell application "Music" to get name of current track'
```

**Play/Pause (app-agnostic):**
```bash
osascript -e 'tell application "Music" to playpause'
# OR for Spotify:
osascript -e 'tell application "Spotify" to playpause'
```

---

### 9. Linux Implementation Patterns

**Volume control via pactl (PulseAudio):**
```bash
pactl set-sink-volume @DEFAULT_SINK@ 50%
pactl set-sink-volume @DEFAULT_SINK@ +5%
pactl set-sink-mute @DEFAULT_SINK@ toggle
```

**Volume control via amixer (ALSA):**
```bash
amixer -D pulse sset Master 50%
amixer -D pulse sset Master 5%+
amixer -D pulse sset Master toggle
```

**Now-playing via playerctl (MPRIS):**
```bash
playerctl metadata --format '{{ artist }} - {{ title }}'
playerctl status
playerctl play-pause
playerctl next / playerctl previous
```

```yaml
---
# Media / AV CLI tools role
# Tools: ffmpeg, ImageMagick, exiftool, libvips
# ffmpeg is also vhs's runtime dependency — see dot_ansible/roles/devtools/
# tasks/main.yml `# --- vhs ---` block.
#
# noRoot=true on Linux: the upstream run_onchange script injects
# `--skip-tags sudo`, which strips the apt block below (it carries
# `tags: [sudo]`). No extra in-role guard needed; user-level fallbacks
# would be impractical for these packages (ffmpeg / imagemagick / libvips
# all want C compilers + system codecs).

# =============================================================================
# macOS — all via Homebrew
# =============================================================================

- name: Install media/AV tools (macOS)
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
  community.general.homebrew:
    name:
      - ffmpeg        # provides ffmpeg, ffprobe, ffplay
      - imagemagick   # v7 unified `magick` binary (also ships `convert` shim)
      - exiftool
      - vips          # provides vips, vipsthumbnail, vipsedit
    state: present

# =============================================================================
# Linux (Debian/Ubuntu) — apt
# =============================================================================

- name: Install media/AV tools from apt (Debian/Ubuntu)
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
  become: true
  tags: [sudo]
  ansible.builtin.apt:
    name:
      - ffmpeg                       # ffmpeg + ffprobe + ffplay
      - imagemagick                  # Ubuntu 24.04 ships v6 → /usr/bin/convert
      - libimage-exiftool-perl       # provides /usr/bin/exiftool
      - libvips-tools                # vips, vipsthumbnail, vipsedit
    state: present
    update_cache: false
```

**Key features for a simple cross-platform role:**

- **macOS block** (when: `ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"`): Homebrew installs
- **Linux block** (when: `ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"`): apt installs with `become: true` + `tags: [sudo]`
- **No role defaults needed** (media_tools has no `defaults/main.yml`) — the tag-based gating at the playbook level is sufficient
- **Ansible OS family mapping:**
  - `Darwin` = macOS
  - `Debian` = Ubuntu/Debian
  - `RedHat` = CentOS/RHEL

```md
# Cross-platform system audio / media control helpers (`sys*`)

## Context

The user wants a CLI-driven way to control **system volume, mute, multimedia playback, and "what's playing"** on both macOS and Linux — primarily so `fleet` can do things like a **remote one-key mute** across all hosts. Today the repo has **no** system-audio helper (`29_media.sh` is file-processing ffmpeg/ImageMagick, not playback; `playerctl` is only referenced inside `56_linux_apps.sh.tmpl`'s responsiveness probe).

Design decisions confirmed with the user:
- **Naming**: `sys*` prefix — `sysvol`, `sysmute`, `sysplay`, `sysnow`.
- **Scope**: full — volume + mute + playback control + now-playing query.
- **fleet**: plain shell functions invoked via `fleet exec --login` (matches the `app-*` precedent; no new executable/completion surface).
- **Two-tier** per the user's "如果關聯的工具較多就做成 init 選項" request:
  - **Built-in tier (always deployed, no opt-in)**: volume/mute fully covered everywhere; playback + now-playing best-effort with OS built-ins, degrading gracefully.
  - **Extended tier (init opt-in → ansible role)**: installs the extra CLIs that unlock full playback control + reliable now-playing; if not selected, only built-ins are used.

The whole thing mirrors the existing **`app-*` helper pattern** (`54_macos_apps.sh.tmpl` / `56_linux_apps.sh.tmpl`): two OS-gated POSIX shell files, `_prefix_guard_os` guards, public bare verbs, graceful fallback.

### Capability matrix (drives built-in vs extended split)

| Verb | macOS built-in | macOS extended | Linux built-in | Linux extended |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sysvol` get/set/±N | `osascript` ✅ | — | `wpctl`/`pactl`/`amixer` ✅ | — |
| `sysmute` on/off/toggle | `osascript` ✅ | — | `wpctl`/`pactl`/`amixer` ✅ | — |
| `sysplay` play-pause/next/prev | per-app AppleScript (Music/Spotify if running) ⚠ | `nowplaying-cli` (any app) ✅ | — (hint) | `playerctl` (MPRIS) ✅ |
| `sysnow` what's playing | per-app AppleScript ⚠ | `nowplaying-cli get` ⚠* | — (hint) | `playerctl metadata` ✅ |

\* **macOS now-playing caveat**: Apple locked the MediaRemote private framework in macOS 15.4+; this host is **26.2**, so `nowplaying-cli get` may return empty. Functions must degrade to per-app AppleScript and print a one-line caveat rather than silently failing. (Documented, not worked around — the [`mediaremote-adapter`](https://github.com/ungive/mediaremote-adapter) bridge is out of scope for v1.)

---

## Implementation

### 1. Built-in tier — two OS-gated shell helpers

Mirror `54_macos_apps.sh.tmpl` / `56_linux_apps.sh.tmpl` conventions exactly: `# shellcheck shell=sh`, OS template gate, `_sysaudio_*` private guards/helpers, `-h|--help` case per verb, `printf` (not `echo`), exit codes + stderr hints.

**`dot_config/shell/57_macos_audio.sh.tmpl`** — gate `{{- if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" -}}`
- `_sysaudio_guard_darwin`, `_sysaudio_have() { command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; }`
- `sysvol [N|+N|-N]` — no arg prints `output volume of (get volume settings)`; `N` → `set volume output volume N`; `±N` reads current then clamps 0–100.
- `sysmute [on|off|toggle]` — default `toggle`; `set volume output muted (true|false|not current)`. **This is the remote-mute primitive.**
- `sysplay [next|previous|""]` — extended: `nowplaying-cli {next|previous|togglePlayPause}` if present; else per-app AppleScript to whichever of Music/Spotify is running (`tell application "X" to playpause`/`next track`); else stderr hint.
- `sysnow` — extended `nowplaying-cli get` (guard empty output → fall through); else per-app AppleScript `name`/`artist of current track`; else hint pointing at the init opt-in. Print the MediaRemote caveat when empty.
- (optional) device switching deferred — only via `SwitchAudioSource` (extended); mention in `--help`, not a core verb in v1.

**`dot_config/shell/57_linux_audio.sh.tmpl`** — gate `{{- if eq .chezmoi.os "linux" -}}`
- `_sysaudio_sink_backend()` — caches first hit of `wpctl` → `pactl` → `amixer` (richest first). `pactl` chosen as the common case (works on both PulseAudio and PipeWire via `pipewire-pulse`).
- `sysvol [N|+N|-N]` / `sysmute [on|off|toggle]` — dispatch on backend:
  - wpctl: `get-volume`/`set-volume @DEFAULT_AUDIO_SINK@ N%`/`set-mute … toggle`
  - pactl: `get-sink-volume`/`set-sink-volume @DEFAULT_SINK@ N%`/`set-sink-mute @DEFAULT_SINK@ toggle`
  - amixer: `get Master`/`set Master N%`/`set Master toggle`
- `sysplay [next|previous|""]` / `sysnow` — `playerctl` (extended). ## Design overview

A **two-tier `sys*` audio/media helper**, mirroring the repo's existing `app-*` pattern:

**Built-in tier (always deployed, zero opt-in)** — two OS-gated POSIX shell files at `dot_config/shell/57_{macos,linux}_audio.sh.tmpl`:
- `sysvol [N|+N|-N]` · `sysmute [on|off|toggle]` · `sysplay [next|prev]` · `sysnow`
- macOS → `osascript`; Linux → auto-detected `wpctl`/`pactl`/`amixer` backend
- **Volume + mute are fully built-in everywhere** (this is your remote-mute primitive); playback/now-playing degrade gracefully when extended tools are absent.

**Extended tier (init opt-in `installMediaControl` → ansible `media_control` role)**:
- macOS: `nowplaying-cli` + `switchaudio-osx`; Linux: `playerctl` + `pulseaudio-utils`
- Unlocks full `sysplay`/`sysnow`; **if not selected, only built-ins are used** — exactly your requirement.

**fleet remote mute**: `fleet exec --login --group all -- sysmute on` (functions load via rc files; lightweight, no new executable/completion surface).

## Two things I flagged as real caveats
1. **macOS now-playing is degraded** — Apple locked the MediaRemote framework in 15.4+, and this host is **26.2**, so `nowplaying-cli get` may return empty. The plan degrades to per-app AppleScript and documents it rather than silently failing.
2. **Linux `sysplay`/`sysnow` over SSH** need a D-Bus session bus (often missing in background SSH) — `sysvol`/`sysmute` are unaffected.

I kept tv channels and the `mediaremote-adapter` bridge out of v1 (noted as follow-ups) to keep scope focused.

## Approved Plan:
# Cross-platform system audio / media control helpers (`sys*`)

## Context

The user wants a CLI-driven way to control **system volume, mute, multimedia playback, and "what's playing"** on both macOS and Linux — primarily so `fleet` can do things like a **remote one-key mute** across all hosts. Today the repo has **no** system-audio helper (`29_media.sh` is file-processing ffmpeg/ImageMagick, not playback; `playerctl` is only referenced inside `56_linux_apps.sh.tmpl`'s responsiveness probe).

Design decisions confirmed with the user:
- **Naming**: `sys*` prefix — `sysvol`, `sysmute`, `sysplay`, `sysnow`.
- **Scope**: full — volume + mute + playback control + now-playing query.
- **fleet**: plain shell functions invoked via `fleet exec --login` (matches the `app-*` precedent; no new executable/completion surface).
- **Two-tier** per the user's "如果關聯的工具較多就做成 init 選項" request:
  - **Built-in tier (always deployed, no opt-in)**: volume/mute fully covered everywhere; playback + now-playing best-effort with OS built-ins, degrading gracefully.
  - **Extended tier (init opt-in → ansible role)**: installs the extra CLIs that unlock full playback control + reliable now-playing; if not selected, only built-ins are used.

The whole thing mirrors the existing **`app-*` helper pattern** (`54_macos_apps.sh.tmpl` / `56_linux_apps.sh.tmpl`): two OS-gated POSIX shell files, `_prefix_guard_os` guards, public bare verbs, graceful fallback.

### Capability matrix (drives built-in vs extended split)

| Verb | macOS built-in | macOS extended | Linux built-in | Linux extended |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sysvol` get/set/±N | `osascript` ✅ | — | `wpctl`/`pactl`/`amixer` ✅ | — |
| `sysmute` on/off/toggle | `osascript` ✅ | — | `wpctl`/`pactl`/`amixer` ✅ | — |
| `sysplay` play-pause/next/prev | per-app AppleScript (Music/Spotify if running) ⚠ | `nowplaying-cli` (any app) ✅ | — (hint) | `playerctl` (MPRIS) ✅ |
| `sysnow` what's playing | per-app AppleScript ⚠ | `nowplaying-cli get` ⚠* | — (hint) | `playerctl metadata` ✅ |

\* **macOS now-playing caveat**: Apple locked the MediaRemote private framework in macOS 15.4+; this host is **26.2**, so `nowplaying-cli get` may return empty. Functions must degrade to per-app AppleScript and print a one-line caveat rather than silently failing. (Documented, not worked around — the [`mediaremote-adapter`](https://github.com/ungive/mediaremote-adapter) bridge is out of scope for v1.)

---

### 1. Built-in tier — two OS-gated shell helpers

Mirror `54_macos_apps.sh.tmpl` / `56_linux_apps.sh.tmpl` conventions exactly: `# shellcheck shell=sh`, OS template gate, `_sysaudio_*` private guards/helpers, `-h|--help` case per verb, `printf` (not `echo`), exit codes + stderr hints.

**`dot_config/shell/57_macos_audio.sh.tmpl`** — gate `{{- if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" -}}`
- `_sysaudio_guard_darwin`, `_sysaudio_have() { command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; }`
- `sysvol [N|+N|-N]` — no arg prints `output volume of (get volume settings)`; `N` → `set volume output volume N`; `±N` reads current then clamps 0–100.
- `sysmute [on|off|toggle]` — default `toggle`; `set volume output muted (true|false|not current)`. **This is the remote-mute primitive.**
- `sysplay [next|previous|""]` — extended: `nowplaying-cli {next|previous|togglePlayPause}` if present; else per-app AppleScript to whichever of Music/Spotify is running (`tell application "X" to playpause`/`next track`); else stderr hint.
- `sysnow` — extended `nowplaying-cli get` (guard empty output → fall through); else per-app AppleScript `name`/`artist of current track`; else hint pointing at the init opt-in. Print the MediaRemote caveat when empty.
- (optional) device switching deferred — only via `SwitchAudioSource` (extended); mention in `--help`, not a core verb in v1.

**`dot_config/shell/57_linux_audio.sh.tmpl`** — gate `{{- if eq .chezmoi.os "linux" -}}`

3	# app-* helpers — graceful control of macOS GUI apps via osascript / Apple Events.
4	#
5	# Why not `killall`? `killall AppName` sends SIGTERM and most GUI apps don't
6	# register a handler, so containers / unsaved buffers / background sync just
7	# die. `osascript -e 'tell application "X" to quit'` sends the Quit Apple
8	# Event — the same thing ⌘Q does — so the app tears down cleanly. Matters
9	# for OrbStack / Docker Desktop / Slack / any app with state.
10	#
11	# Frozen-app detection (`appresponsive`) is best-effort: macOS exposes the
12	# "Not Responding" flag only via Activity Monitor's private SPI. The public
13	# proxy is "send a no-op Apple Event with a short timeout — if it throws,
14	# the app is hung." False positives happen on apps mid-launch.
15	#
16	# All helpers take an app NAME (e.g. `OrbStack`, `Google Chrome`), not a
17	# bundle ID. `$1` is passed via osascript's `argv` so spaces and quotes in
18	# app names are handled correctly without shell-escaping gymnastics.
19	#
20	# Linux counterpart: dot_config/shell/56_linux_apps.sh.tmpl. Same public
21	# verb names (appquit / applaunch / appactivate / apprestart / apprunning /
22	# applist / appresponsive) but a different backend — gtk-launch + pkill -TERM
23	# + optional GNOME window-calls extension. Cross-platform muscle memory by
24	# design; per-platform gaps documented in
25	# backlog/linux-desktop-app-control.md (Alt+H "hide" is mac-only — Linux
26	# can't hide windows without compositor IPC).
27	
28	_macapp_is_darwin() { [ "$(uname -s 2>/dev/null)" = "Darwin" ]; }
29	
30	_macapp_guard_darwin() {
31	    if ! _macapp_is_darwin; then
32	        printf 'app-helper: macOS-only (current OS: %s)\n' \
33	            "$(uname -s 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)" >&2
34	        return 1
35	    fi
36	}
37	
38	_macapp_need_name() {
39	    if [ -z "$1" ]; then
40	        printf 'usage: %s <AppName>\n  e.g. %s OrbStack\n' "$2" "$2" >&2
41	        return 2
42	    fi
43	}
44	
45	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
46	# Public: lifecycle
47	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
48	
49	# appquit NAME — send Quit Apple Event (graceful, equivalent to ⌘Q).
50	appquit() {
51	    case "$1" in -h|--help)
52	        printf 'usage: appquit <AppName>\n  Send Quit Apple Event (graceful shutdown).\n  Example: appquit OrbStack\n'
53	        return 0 ;;
54	    esac
55	    _macapp_guard_darwin || return 1
56	    _macapp_need_name "$1" appquit || return 2
57	    osascript \

59	        -e 'tell application (item 1 of argv) to quit' \
60	        -e 'end run' \
61	        -- "$1"
62	}
63	
64	# applaunch NAME — start the app in the background (no focus steal).
65	applaunch() {
66	    case "$1" in -h|--help)
67	        printf 'usage: applaunch <AppName>\n  Launch in background (no focus steal). Use appactivate to bring to front.\n'

69	    esac
70	    _macapp_guard_darwin || return 1
71	    _macapp_need_name "$1" applaunch || return 2
72	    osascript \
73	        -e 'on run argv' \
74	        -e 'tell application (item 1 of argv) to launch' \
75	        -e 'end run' \
76	        -- "$1"
77	}
78	
79	# appactivate NAME — start (if needed) and bring to front.
80	appactivate() {
81	    case "$1" in -h|--help)
82	        printf 'usage: appactivate <AppName>\n  Launch + bring to front. Use applaunch for headless start.\n'
83	        return 0 ;;
84	    esac
85	    _macapp_guard_darwin || return 1
86	    _macapp_need_name "$1" appactivate || return 2
87	    osascript \
88	        -e 'on run argv' \
89	        -e 'tell application (item 1 of argv) to activate' \
90	        -e 'end run' \
91	        -- "$1"
92	}
93	
94	# apprestart NAME — quit, wait for shutdown, relaunch in background.
95	apprestart() {
96	    case "$1" in -h|--help)
97	        printf 'usage: apprestart <AppName>\n  Graceful quit + background relaunch. Useful after config edits.\n'
98	        return 0 ;;
99	    esac
100	    _macapp_guard_darwin || return 1
101	    _macapp_need_name "$1" apprestart || return 2
102	    appquit "$1" || return $?
103	    # Poll until really gone — `quit` returns before the app process exits.
104	    _macapp_i=0
105	    while [ "$_macapp_i" -lt 30 ] && apprunning "$1"; do
106	        sleep 0.5
107	        _macapp_i=$((_macapp_i + 1))
108	    done
109	    unset _macapp_i
110	    applaunch "$1"
111	}
112	
113	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
114	# Public: inspection
115	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
116	
117	# apprunning NAME — exit 0 if app is running, 1 otherwise. Silent.
118	apprunning() {
119	    case "$1" in -h|--help)
120	        printf 'usage: apprunning <AppName>\n  Exit 0 if running, 1 otherwise. Silent — use $? or && / ||.\n'
121	        return 0 ;;
122	    esac
123	    _macapp_guard_darwin || return 1
124	    _macapp_need_name "$1" apprunning || return 2
125	    _macapp_out=$(osascript \
126	        -e 'on run argv' \
127	        -e 'tell application "System Events" to return (exists (processes where name is (item 1 of argv)))' \
128	        -e 'end run' \
129	        -- "$1" 2>/dev/null)
130	    [ "$_macapp_out" = "true" ]
131	}
132	
133	# applist [--pids] — list visible (foreground) GUI apps, one per line.
134	# Default: just names. `--pids` adds PID + bundle path.
135	applist() {
136	    case "$1" in -h|--help)
137	        printf 'usage: applist [--pids|--all]\n'
138	        printf '  Default     names of visible foreground GUI apps, one per line.\n'
139	        printf '  --pids      "<pid>\\t<name>" via lsappinfo (foreground only).\n'
140	        printf '  --all       include background-only / agent processes.\n'
141	        return 0 ;;
142	    esac
143	    _macapp_guard_darwin || return 1
144	
145	    case "${1:-}" in
146	        --pids)
147	            # AppleScript exposes `unix id` directly — cleaner than parsing
148	            # `lsappinfo list` (which is multi-line and includes background
149	            # daemons mixed with foreground apps).
150	            osascript \
151	                -e 'tell application "System Events"' \
152	                -e '  set out to ""' \
153	                -e '  repeat with p in (every application process whose background only is false)' \
154	                -e '    set out to out & (unix id of p) & tab & (name of p) & linefeed' \
155	                -e '  end repeat' \
156	                -e '  return out' \
157	                -e 'end tell'
158	            ;;
159	        --all)
160	            osascript \
161	                -e 'tell application "System Events" to set procNames to name of every process' \
162	                -e 'set AppleScript'\''s text item delimiters to linefeed' \
163	                -e 'return procNames as text'
164	            ;;
165	        ""|*)
166	            osascript \
167	                -e 'tell application "System Events" to set procNames to name of every application process whose background only is false' \
168	                -e 'set AppleScript'\''s text item delimiters to linefeed' \
169	                -e 'return procNames as text'
170	            ;;
171	    esac
172	}
173	
174	# appresponsive NAME [TIMEOUT_SEC] — exit 0 if app responds within timeout.
175	# Sends a no-op Get-name Apple Event with `with timeout`. If AppleScript
176	# throws (timeout or "isn't running"), exit 1.
177	#
178	# Best-effort: this is the public-API proxy for "Not Responding". An app
179	# mid-launch may falsely fail; raise TIMEOUT (default 2s) to reduce noise.
180	appresponsive() {
181	    case "$1" in -h|--help)
182	        printf 'usage: appresponsive <AppName> [TIMEOUT_SEC]\n'
183	        printf '  Exit 0 if app answers an Apple Event within TIMEOUT (default 2s).\n'
184	        printf '  Exit 1 if hung, not running, or scripting-disabled.\n'
185	        printf '  Example: appresponsive OrbStack 5 || echo hung\n'
186	        return 0 ;;
187	    esac
188	    _macapp_guard_darwin || return 1
189	    _macapp_need_name "$1" appresponsive || return 2
190	    _macapp_to=${2:-2}
191	    apprunning "$1" || return 1
192	    _macapp_out=$(osascript \
193	        -e 'on run argv' \
194	        -e 'set t to (item 2 of argv) as integer' \
195	        -e 'with timeout of t seconds' \
196	        -e '  try' \
197	        -e '    tell application (item 1 of argv) to get name' \
198	        -e '    return "yes"' \
199	        -e '  on error' \
200	        -e '    return "no"' \
201	        -e '  end try' \
202	        -e 'end timeout' \
203	        -e 'end run' \
204	        -- "$1" "$_macapp_to" 2>/dev/null)
205	    unset _macapp_to
206	    [ "$_macapp_out" = "yes" ]
207	}

209	{{ end -}}

1	# 56_clipboard_history.sh — cross-platform clipboard-history helpers.
2	#
3	# Wraps Maccy (macOS, plaintext SQLite) and CopyQ (Linux, shipped CLI) behind
4	# a unified `cb` / `cbl` / `cbe` API. Replaces the Raycast-specific helper
5	# deleted in 2026-05 — Raycast 1.7+ encrypts its DB with SQLCipher and the
6	# key cannot be recovered without binary RE; see
7	# pitfalls/raycast-clipboard-sqlcipher-key-not-recoverable.md.
8	#
9	# Backend selection (override autodetect with CLIP_BACKEND=copyq|maccy):
10	#   macOS:  prefer Maccy SQLite, fall back to CopyQ if installed manually.
11	#   Linux:  CopyQ only.
12	# No backend → one-line install hint to stderr (ubuntu_server typical case).
13	#
14	# Maccy schema (verified against p0deje/Maccy@master HistoryItem.swift +
15	# HistoryItemContent.swift, 2026-05):
16	#   ZHISTORYITEM(Z_PK, ZAPPLICATION, ZFIRSTCOPIEDAT, ZLASTCOPIEDAT,
17	#                ZNUMBEROFCOPIES, ZPIN, ZTITLE)
18	#   ZHISTORYITEMCONTENT(Z_PK, ZTYPE, ZVALUE, ZITEM -> ZHISTORYITEM.Z_PK)
19	# Core Data dates are seconds since 2001-01-01; add 978307200 for Unix epoch.
20

23	_clip_maccy_path() {
24	    p="$HOME/Library/Application Support/Maccy/Storage.sqlite"
25	    [ -f "$p" ] && { printf 'maccy:%s\n' "$p"; return 0; }
26	    p="$HOME/Library/Containers/org.p0deje.Maccy/Data/Library/Application Support/Maccy/Storage.sqlite"
27	    [ -f "$p" ] && { printf 'maccy:%s\n' "$p"; return 0; }
28	    return 1
29	}

31	_clip_copyq_ready() {
32	    command -v copyq >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
33	    copyq size >/dev/null 2>&1
34	}
35	
36	_clip_backend() {
37	    case "${CLIP_BACKEND:-}" in
38	        copyq) _clip_copyq_ready && echo copyq ;;
39	        maccy) _clip_maccy_path ;;
40	        '')
41	            if [ "$(uname)" = "Darwin" ]; then
42	                _clip_maccy_path && return 0
43	                _clip_copyq_ready && echo copyq

```tmpl
{{- if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" -}}
# shellcheck shell=sh
# sys* helpers — control system audio + media playback from the shell (macOS).
#
# Two tiers, autodetected at call time:
#   built-in (always works) — volume + mute via `osascript` (Apple Events).
#                             play/pause + now-playing via per-app AppleScript
#                             to whichever of Music/Spotify is running.
#   extended (opt-in)       — `nowplaying-cli` gives app-agnostic transport +
#                             now-playing; `SwitchAudioSource` switches output
#                             device. Installed by the `media_control` ansible
#                             role (chezmoi init: installMediaControl=true).
#
# ⚠ now-playing caveat: Apple locked the private MediaRemote framework in
# macOS 15.4+, so `nowplaying-cli get` returns empty on current macOS. `sysnow`
# degrades to per-app AppleScript (Music/Spotify only — not Safari/Chrome web
# audio) and prints a one-line caveat rather than failing silently.
#
# Linux counterpart: dot_config/shell/57_linux_audio.sh.tmpl. SAME public verb
# names (sysvol / sysmute / sysplay / sysnow) for cross-platform muscle memory;
# backends diverge (osascript here vs wpctl/pactl/amixer + playerctl there).
#
# fleet: `fleet exec --login --group all -- sysmute on` for a remote one-key
# mute (--login so rc files load these functions). Docs: docs/tools/media-control.md

_sysaudio_is_darwin() { [ "$(uname -s 2>/dev/null)" = "Darwin" ]; }
_sysaudio_have() { command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; }

_sysaudio_guard_darwin() {
    if ! _sysaudio_is_darwin; then
        printf 'sys-audio: macOS-only (current OS: %s)\n' \
            "$(uname -s 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)" >&2
        return 1
    fi
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Public: volume + mute (fully built-in — no extra tools needed)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# sysvol [N|+N|-N] — get (no arg) or set output volume (0-100). ± is relative.
sysvol() {
    case "$1" in -h|--help)
        printf 'usage: sysvol [N|+N|-N]\n'
        printf '  no arg   print current output volume (0-100)\n'
        printf '  N        set absolute volume (clamped 0-100)\n'
        printf '  +N / -N  adjust relative to current\n'
        return 0 ;;
    esac
    _sysaudio_guard_darwin || return 1

    _sysaudio_cur=$(osascript -e 'output volume of (get volume settings)' 2>/dev/null)
    if [ -z "$1" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$_sysaudio_cur"
        unset _sysaudio_cur
        return 0
    fi

    case "$1" in
        +*) _sysaudio_new=$((_sysaudio_cur + ${1#+})) ;;
        -*) _sysaudio_new=$((_sysaudio_cur - ${1#-})) ;;
        ''|*[!0-9]*)
            printf 'sysvol: not a number: %s\n' "$1" >&2
            unset _sysaudio_cur
            return 2 ;;
        *) _sysaudio_new=$1 ;;
    esac
    [ "$_sysaudio_new" -lt 0 ] && _sysaudio_new=0
    [ "$_sysaudio_new" -gt 100 ] && _sysaudio_new=100
    osascript -e "set volume output volume $_sysaudio_new"
    unset _sysaudio_cur _sysaudio_new
}

# sysmute [on|off|toggle] — mute the system output. Default: toggle.
# This is the remote one-key mute primitive (fleet exec --login -- sysmute on).
sysmute() {
    case "$1" in -h|--help)
        printf 'usage: sysmute [on|off|toggle]\n  Default toggle. Remote: fleet exec --login -- sysmute on\n'
        return 0 ;;
    esac
    _sysaudio_guard_darwin || return 1
    case "${1:-toggle}" in
        on|1|true)   osascript -e 'set volume output muted true' ;;
        off|0|false) osascript -e 'set volume output muted false' ;;
        toggle)      osascript -e 'set volume output muted (not (output muted of (get volume settings)))' ;;
        *) printf 'sysmute: expected on|off|toggle, got: %s\n' "$1" >&2; return 2 ;;
    esac
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Public: playback + now-playing (built-in per-app; richer with nowplaying-cli)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# _sysaudio_running_player — echo "Music" or "Spotify" if one is running, else nothing.
_sysaudio_running_player() {
    for _sysaudio_app in Spotify Music; do
        _sysaudio_r=$(osascript \
            -e 'on run argv' \
            -e 'tell application "System Events" to return (exists (processes where name is (item 1 of argv)))' \
            -e 'end run' \
            -- "$_sysaudio_app" 2>/dev/null)
        if [ "$_sysaudio_r" = "true" ]; then
            printf '%s\n' "$_sysaudio_app"
            unset _sysaudio_app _sysaudio_r
            return 0
        fi
    done
    unset _sysaudio_app _sysaudio_r
    return 1
}

# sysplay [next|previous|prev] — toggle play/pause (default) or skip track.
sysplay() {
    case "$1" in -h|--help)
        printf 'usage: sysplay [next|previous|prev]\n  No arg toggles play/pause. Built-in covers Music/Spotify;\n  nowplaying-cli (installMediaControl) covers any app.\n'
        return 0 ;;
    esac
    _sysaudio_guard_darwin || return 1

    if _sysaudio_have nowplaying-cli; then
        case "${1:-}" in
            next)            nowplaying-cli next ;;
            previous|prev)   nowplaying-cli previous ;;
            '')              nowplaying-cli togglePlayPause ;;
            *) printf 'sysplay: expected next|previous, got: %s\n' "$1" >&2; return 2 ;;
        esac
        return $?
    fi

    # built-in fallback: drive whichever player is running
    _sysaudio_app=$(_sysaudio_running_player) || {
        printf 'sysplay: no Music/Spotify running. For app-agnostic control:\n' >&2
        printf '  chezmoi init with installMediaControl=true (installs nowplaying-cli)\n' >&2
        return 1
    }
    case "${1:-}" in
        next)          osascript -e "tell application \"$_sysaudio_app\" to next track" ;;
        previous|prev) osascript -e "tell application \"$_sysaudio_app\" to previous track" ;;
        '')            osascript -e "tell application \"$_sysaudio_app\" to playpause" ;;
        *) printf 'sysplay: expected next|previous, got: %s\n' "$1" >&2; unset _sysaudio_app; return 2 ;;
    esac
    unset _sysaudio_app
}

# sysnow — print what's currently playing ("Artist - Title").
sysnow() {
    case "$1" in -h|--help)
        printf 'usage: sysnow\n  Print the currently playing track. macOS 15.4+ locked the\n  MediaRemote API, so this covers Music/Spotify only (not web audio).\n'
        return 0 ;;
    esac
    _sysaudio_guard_darwin || return 1

    # extended: nowplaying-cli (may return empty on macOS 15.4+ — guard it)
    if _sysaudio_have nowplaying-cli; then
        _sysaudio_title=$(nowplaying-cli get title 2>/dev/null)
        if [ -n "$_sysaudio_title" ] && [ "$_sysaudio_title" != "null" ]; then
            _sysaudio_artist=$(nowplaying-cli get artist 2>/dev/null)
            [ "$_sysaudio_artist" = "null" ] && _sysaudio_artist=
            if [ -n "$_sysaudio_artist" ]; then
                printf '%s - %s\n' "$_sysaudio_artist" "$_sysaudio_title"
            else
                printf '%s\n' "$_sysaudio_title"
            fi
            unset _sysaudio_title _sysaudio_artist
            return 0
        fi
        unset _sysaudio_title
        # fall through: MediaRemote locked on this macOS — try per-app
    fi

    # built-in fallback: per-app AppleScript
    _sysaudio_app=$(_sysaudio_running_player) || {
        printf 'sysnow: nothing detected (no Music/Spotify running).\n' >&2
        printf '  macOS 15.4+ locks system-wide now-playing; web/other apps are not visible.\n' >&2
        return 1
    }
    _sysaudio_state=$(osascript -e "tell application \"$_sysaudio_app\" to player state as text" 2>/dev/null)
    if [ "$_sysaudio_state" != "playing" ] && [ "$_sysaudio_state" != "paused" ]; then
        printf '%s: stopped\n' "$_sysaudio_app"
        unset _sysaudio_app _sysaudio_state
        return 0
    fi
    _sysaudio_title=$(osascript -e "tell application \"$_sysaudio_app\" to name of current track" 2>/dev/null)
    _sysaudio_artist=$(osascript -e "tell application \"$_sysaudio_app\" to artist of current track" 2>/dev/null)
    if [ -n "$_sysaudio_artist" ]; then
        printf '%s - %s\n' "$_sysaudio_artist" "$_sysaudio_title"
    else
        printf '%s\n' "$_sysaudio_title"
    fi
    unset _sysaudio_app _sysaudio_state _sysaudio_title _sysaudio_artist
}

{{ end -}}

```tmpl
{{- if eq .chezmoi.os "linux" -}}
# shellcheck shell=sh
# sys* helpers — control system audio + media playback from the shell (Linux).
#
# Linux counterpart to dot_config/shell/57_macos_audio.sh.tmpl. SAME public verb
# names (sysvol / sysmute / sysplay / sysnow) for cross-platform muscle memory;
# backends diverge by necessity.
#
# Two tiers, autodetected at call time:
#   built-in (volume/mute) — first available of wpctl (PipeWire) → pactl
#                            (Pulse, also fronts PipeWire via pipewire-pulse) →
#                            amixer (ALSA). pactl ships with pulseaudio-utils.
#   extended (playback)    — `playerctl` (MPRIS over D-Bus) drives play/pause/
#                            next and reads now-playing for any compliant player
#                            (Spotify/VLC/mpv/Firefox/Chrome). Installed by the
#                            `media_control` ansible role (installMediaControl=true).
#
# ⚠ D-Bus-over-SSH caveat: sysplay/sysnow need DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS, which
# background SSH sessions usually lack — so `fleet exec` can mute (sysvol/sysmute
# go through wpctl/pactl, unaffected) but may not drive playback. Docs:
# docs/tools/media-control.md

_sysaudio_is_linux() { [ "$(uname -s 2>/dev/null)" = "Linux" ]; }
_sysaudio_have() { command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; }

_sysaudio_guard_linux() {
    if ! _sysaudio_is_linux; then
        printf 'sys-audio: Linux-only (current OS: %s)\n' \
            "$(uname -s 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)" >&2
        return 1
    fi
}

# _sysaudio_backend — echo the first available mixer backend (cached per shell).
# Override with SYSAUDIO_BACKEND=wpctl|pactl|amixer.
_sysaudio_backend() {
    if [ -n "${SYSAUDIO_BACKEND:-}" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$SYSAUDIO_BACKEND"
        return 0
    fi
    if [ -z "${_sysaudio_backend_cache:-}" ]; then
        if _sysaudio_have wpctl; then _sysaudio_backend_cache=wpctl
        elif _sysaudio_have pactl; then _sysaudio_backend_cache=pactl
        elif _sysaudio_have amixer; then _sysaudio_backend_cache=amixer
        else _sysaudio_backend_cache=none
        fi
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "$_sysaudio_backend_cache"
    [ "$_sysaudio_backend_cache" != none ]
}

_sysaudio_backend_hint() {
    printf 'sys-audio: no mixer backend (wpctl/pactl/amixer) found.\n' >&2
    printf '  sudo apt install pulseaudio-utils   # provides pactl (works on PipeWire too)\n' >&2
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Public: volume + mute (built-in)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# sysvol [N|+N|-N] — get (no arg) or set output volume (0-100). ± is relative.
sysvol() {
    case "$1" in -h|--help)
        printf 'usage: sysvol [N|+N|-N]\n'
        printf '  no arg   print current output volume (0-100)\n'
        printf '  N        set absolute volume (0-100)\n'
        printf '  +N / -N  adjust relative to current\n'
        return 0 ;;
    esac
    _sysaudio_guard_linux || return 1
    _sysaudio_be=$(_sysaudio_backend) || { _sysaudio_backend_hint; return 1; }

    # --- get (no arg) ---
    if [ -z "$1" ]; then
        case "$_sysaudio_be" in
            wpctl)  wpctl get-volume @DEFAULT_AUDIO_SINK@ 2>/dev/null | awk '{printf "%d\n", $2*100}' ;;
            pactl)  pactl get-sink-volume @DEFAULT_SINK@ 2>/dev/null | grep -o '[0-9]\{1,3\}%' | head -1 | tr -d '%' ;;
            amixer) amixer get Master 2>/dev/null | grep -o '[0-9]\{1,3\}%' | head -1 | tr -d '%' ;;
        esac
        unset _sysaudio_be
        return 0
    fi

    # --- set / adjust ---
    case "$1" in
        +*) _sysaudio_dir=up;   _sysaudio_mag=${1#+} ;;
        -*) _sysaudio_dir=down; _sysaudio_mag=${1#-} ;;
        *)  _sysaudio_dir=abs;  _sysaudio_mag=$1 ;;
    esac
    case "$_sysaudio_mag" in
        ''|*[!0-9]*) printf 'sysvol: not a number: %s\n' "$1" >&2
                     unset _sysaudio_be _sysaudio_dir _sysaudio_mag; return 2 ;;
    esac
    case "$_sysaudio_be" in
        wpctl)
            case "$_sysaudio_dir" in
                up)   wpctl set-volume -l 1.0 @DEFAULT_AUDIO_SINK@ "${_sysaudio_mag}%+" ;;
                down) wpctl set-volume @DEFAULT_AUDIO_SINK@ "${_sysaudio_mag}%-" ;;
                abs)  wpctl set-volume -l 1.0 @DEFAULT_AUDIO_SINK@ "${_sysaudio_mag}%" ;;
            esac ;;
        pactl)
            case "$_sysaudio_dir" in
                up)   pactl set-sink-volume @DEFAULT_SINK@ "+${_sysaudio_mag}%" ;;
                down) pactl set-sink-volume @DEFAULT_SINK@ "-${_sysaudio_mag}%" ;;
                abs)  pactl set-sink-volume @DEFAULT_SINK@ "${_sysaudio_mag}%" ;;
            esac ;;
        amixer)
            case "$_sysaudio_dir" in
                up)   amixer -q set Master "${_sysaudio_mag}%+" ;;
                down) amixer -q set Master "${_sysaudio_mag}%-" ;;
                abs)  amixer -q set Master "${_sysaudio_mag}%" ;;
            esac ;;
    esac
    unset _sysaudio_be _sysaudio_dir _sysaudio_mag
}

# sysmute [on|off|toggle] — mute the system output. Default: toggle.
# Remote one-key mute primitive: fleet exec --login -- sysmute on
sysmute() {
    case "$1" in -h|--help)
        printf 'usage: sysmute [on|off|toggle]\n  Default toggle. Remote: fleet exec --login -- sysmute on\n'
        return 0 ;;
    esac
    _sysaudio_guard_linux || return 1
    _sysaudio_be=$(_sysaudio_backend) || { _sysaudio_backend_hint; return 1; }
    _sysaudio_act=${1:-toggle}
    case "$_sysaudio_act" in on|1|true) _sysaudio_act=on ;; off|0|false) _sysaudio_act=off ;; toggle) ;; \
        *) printf 'sysmute: expected on|off|toggle, got: %s\n' "$1" >&2; unset _sysaudio_be _sysaudio_act; return 2 ;; esac
    case "$_sysaudio_be" in
        wpctl)  case "$_sysaudio_act" in on) wpctl set-mute @DEFAULT_AUDIO_SINK@ 1 ;; off) wpctl set-mute @DEFAULT_AUDIO_SINK@ 0 ;; toggle) wpctl set-mute @DEFAULT_AUDIO_SINK@ toggle ;; esac ;;
        pactl)  case "$_sysaudio_act" in on) pactl set-sink-mute @DEFAULT_SINK@ 1 ;; off) pactl set-sink-mute @DEFAULT_SINK@ 0 ;; toggle) pactl set-sink-mute @DEFAULT_SINK@ toggle ;; esac ;;
        amixer) case "$_sysaudio_act" in on) amixer -q set Master mute ;; off) amixer -q set Master unmute ;; toggle) amixer -q set Master toggle ;; esac ;;
    esac
    unset _sysaudio_be _sysaudio_act
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Public: playback + now-playing (extended — needs playerctl / MPRIS)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

_sysaudio_playerctl_hint() {
    printf 'sys-audio: playerctl not installed (needed for %s).\n' "$1" >&2
    printf '  chezmoi init with installMediaControl=true, or: sudo apt install playerctl\n' >&2
}

# sysplay [next|previous|prev] — toggle play/pause (default) or skip track.
sysplay() {
    case "$1" in -h|--help)
        printf 'usage: sysplay [next|previous|prev]\n  No arg toggles play/pause via playerctl (MPRIS).\n'
        return 0 ;;
    esac
    _sysaudio_guard_linux || return 1
    _sysaudio_have playerctl || { _sysaudio_playerctl_hint sysplay; return 1; }
    case "${1:-}" in
        next)          playerctl next ;;
        previous|prev) playerctl previous ;;
        '')            playerctl play-pause ;;
        *) printf 'sysplay: expected next|previous, got: %s\n' "$1" >&2; return 2 ;;
    esac
}

# sysnow — print what's currently playing ("Artist - Title") + status.
sysnow() {
    case "$1" in -h|--help)
        printf 'usage: sysnow\n  Print the currently playing track via playerctl (MPRIS).\n'
        return 0 ;;
    esac
    _sysaudio_guard_linux || return 1
    _sysaudio_have playerctl || { _sysaudio_playerctl_hint sysnow; return 1; }
    _sysaudio_status=$(playerctl status 2>/dev/null) || {
        printf 'sysnow: no active MPRIS player.\n' >&2; unset _sysaudio_status; return 1
    }
    _sysaudio_artist=$(playerctl metadata artist 2>/dev/null)
    _sysaudio_title=$(playerctl metadata title 2>/dev/null)
    if [ -n "$_sysaudio_artist" ] && [ -n "$_sysaudio_title" ]; then
        printf '%s - %s [%s]\n' "$_sysaudio_artist" "$_sysaudio_title" "$_sysaudio_status"
    elif [ -n "$_sysaudio_title" ]; then
        printf '%s [%s]\n' "$_sysaudio_title" "$_sysaudio_status"
    else
        printf '%s\n' "$_sysaudio_status"
    fi
    unset _sysaudio_status _sysaudio_artist _sysaudio_title
}

{{ end -}}

```yaml
---
# System media-control role — CLIs that back the sys* shell helpers
# (dot_config/shell/57_{macos,linux}_audio.sh.tmpl: sysvol/sysmute/sysplay/sysnow).
#
# Gated on the installMediaControl chezmoi prompt (tag: media_control). NOT
# installed by default: the built-in tier (sysvol/sysmute via osascript on
# macOS, wpctl/pactl/amixer on Linux) works with zero extra tools. This role
# only adds the *extended* tier — app-agnostic transport + now-playing.
#
# Distinct from the media_tools role (ffmpeg/ImageMagick — file processing).
#
# noRoot=true on Linux: the upstream run_onchange script injects
# `--skip-tags sudo`, stripping the apt block below (it carries `tags: [sudo]`).

# =============================================================================
# macOS — Homebrew
# =============================================================================

- name: Install media-control CLIs (macOS)
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
  community.general.homebrew:
    name:
      - nowplaying-cli     # app-agnostic transport (play/pause/next) + `get`
                           # ⚠ now-playing `get` is empty on macOS 15.4+
                           # (Apple locked MediaRemote); sysnow degrades to
                           # per-app AppleScript. Transport still works.
      - switchaudio-osx    # SwitchAudioSource — list/switch output devices
    state: present

# =============================================================================
# Linux (Debian/Ubuntu) — apt
# =============================================================================

- name: Install media-control CLIs from apt (Debian/Ubuntu)
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
  become: true
  tags: [sudo]
  ansible.builtin.apt:
    name:
      - playerctl          # MPRIS over D-Bus: sysplay/sysnow for any compliant
                           # player (Spotify/VLC/mpv/Firefox/Chrome)
      - pulseaudio-utils   # provides pactl — guarantees a sysvol/sysmute backend
                           # even on a PipeWire box (via pipewire-pulse)
    state: present
    update_cache: false

```
